increments.title: DR1 refuses to move on from the contact page until an address is chosen; the frontend accepts Save and continue with nothing selected.
increments.detail:
Pressing Save and continue with no radio chosen is allowed through. The page only rejects a value that is not one of the addresses offered, and the controller says so in as many words: the contact is mandatory as an obligation, but an empty submit returns the trader to the hub with the task simply incomplete (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/controller.js:29-39). The trader is not told they have skipped anything at the moment they skip it; they find out later at the hub.

DR1 validates the choice on submit and, when nothing is selected, re-renders the page with the error "Select a contact address" in the summary and against the radios (app/routes.js:1138-1155). There is no way past the page without answering it.

Make an empty submit on the contact page an error carrying the message the frontend already has for the case, rather than a silent pass. The message exists — contactRequired, "Select a contact address" — and is only reached today when a value outside the list is posted. Blocking at the page is already this journey's pattern rather than a departure from it: the frontend ships two validators for a radio group, and the origin, destination-country, port-of-exit and declaration pages all use the one that refuses an empty answer, while the contact page uses the permissive one that explicitly allows an empty string (src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:100-121). So the work is one page moving onto the stricter of two validators the codebase already has, and it is not a decision about the whole journey.

FALSIFIED BY: Submitting the frontend contact page with no radio selected and getting "There is a problem" rather than a redirect.

increments.title: DR1 asks for the CPH number as county, parish and holding number in three boxes; the frontend asks for it as one free-text field.
increments.detail:
One text box ten characters wide, hinted "For example, 123456789 or 123/456/789." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/template.njk:11-23). Whatever the trader types has its slashes stripped and must then be exactly nine digits (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:34-42), so the number is stored as nine bare digits and the parts of it are never separated. Nothing on screen says which digits are the county, which the parish and which the holding.

Three boxes side by side under one "CPH number" legend, hinted "For example 12/345/6789" (app/views/partials/cph-number-input.html:14-49). The boxes take two, three and four digits and are labelled County, Parish and Holding number for a screen reader; the labels are hidden from sight, so what a user meets is three boxes sized to the part each takes. Typing enough digits moves the cursor to the next box on its own, non-digits are discarded as they are typed, and the answer is kept and shown in the slashed form — the completed consignment addresses page shows "12/345/6789".

Replace the single field with three numeric inputs of two, three and four digits under one legend and one example hint, and carry the parts through validation so an error can name the box that is wrong rather than the whole number. Decide at the same time what is stored: DR1 keeps the slashed form and shows it back that way, the frontend today keeps nine bare digits, and the stored form is what the consignment addresses page and the check-answers summary display.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding more than one CPH input on the frontend CPH page, or a County or Parish label anywhere in its rendered markup.

increments.title: DR1 lets a user reuse an address already given for another role with one click on the consignment addresses page; the frontend makes them search the address book again for every role.
increments.detail:
Every role on the Consignment addresses page offers exactly one action, Add, which opens that role's address picker. There is no way to say that the consignor is the same as the place of origin, or that the importer or the place of destination is the same as the consignee: the user goes to the picker and finds the same address in the list again. The hub builds one action per row from a single template, so no row can offer a second one (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:32-46).

Once an earlier role is filled, DR1 adds a second action to the roles that can borrow from it, beside the Add link. Consignor gains Same as place of origin; Importer and Place of destination each gain Same as consignee (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:84-101). Pressing one copies the name, address lines and country straight into that role and returns to the page with the address shown. The shortcut appears only while the source role is filled and the target is not, so it never offers a copy there is nothing to copy from and never sits beside an address that has already been chosen.

Give the consignor, importer and place-of-destination rows a second action that copies the already-chosen address into that role and returns to the Consignment addresses page. The frontend already holds each chosen party in the notification's answers, so the copy is a state write and needs no new lookup. Which role borrows from which is fixed by DR1: consignor from place of origin, importer and place of destination from consignee. The action must disappear once the target role has an address of its own, otherwise it overwrites a deliberate choice.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a control anywhere in the frontend that copies one role's address into another — a Same as link on the consignment addresses page, or a party page that arrives with the earlier role's address already selected.

increments.title: DR1 shows the whole chosen address against each role on the consignment addresses page; the frontend shows only the organisation's name.
increments.detail:
Each role is a summary-list row whose value is the chosen party's name and nothing else — the row is built from `parties[party.id]?.name` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:48-53). A trader who has picked one of two similarly named farms cannot tell from this page which one is in the notification; they have to open the picker again to see the street, town, postcode or country. Before anything is chosen the row reads Not added yet.

Each role is a headed section, and a filled one shows the address in an inset block: the name on its own line and then every address line, ending with the postcode and country, with a Change link underneath (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:60-70). The CPH row shows the number itself the same way. The complete-state capture shows all six roles rendered this way, so the page doubles as a check of the addresses without opening anything.

Render the chosen address in full against each filled role rather than the name alone, with the Change action below it. The address lines are already resolved for this page by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/resolve-parties.js, and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js already formats a record into lines, so this is a template change on the hub and not a new lookup. Widening the row also relieves the present layout, where the role name and its hint are squeezed into a narrow summary-list key column and wrap over five or six lines.

increments.title: DR1 offers each address role only the addresses saved for that role; the frontend offers the whole address book on all five party pages and on the contact page.
increments.detail:
All five party pages show the same list. Place of origin, Consignor or exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination each report "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" over the identical thirteen records, so a user choosing a place of origin is offered Tech Imports Ltd and Import Co UK alongside the farms, and a user choosing a consignee is offered Astra Rosales in Switzerland. The contact page offers the same book again, all thirteen as radios, including overseas addresses. This is deliberate today: the address book holds no type, so one search serves every role (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15) and no picker passes a role to it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:35-36).

DR1 records what an address is for when it is saved, and each page shows only the matching records. The place-of-origin capture reports "Showing 9 out of 9 results" and every row is a farm or breeding centre abroad — the whole list is filtered against the role's type aliases (app/routes.js:3441-3465). Consignor or exporter also accepts records typed consignor or exporter; consignee, importer and place of destination each take their own type. The contact page is filtered separately, to addresses typed as a branch address, and DR1 seeds it with three GB branches of the trader's own business rather than with consignment addresses.

This needs the address book to carry what each address is for before the frontend can filter on it. The API's address contract has no such field — OperatorResponse in the address-book service exposes name, address lines, country, phone, email and the soft-delete flag and nothing role-shaped — so the contract, the store and the INS frontend's add form all have to gain it first. Only then can each party page ask for its own role and the contact page ask for branch addresses. Do the five party roles and the contact page in one pass: they read the same book through the same service and would otherwise diverge.

increments.title: DR1 narrows the address list as the user types; the frontend leaves the list alone until Search is pressed and the page reloads.
increments.detail:
The Search box does nothing until the trader presses the Search button beside it, which submits the whole picker form and reloads the page with a new set of rows. Typing narrows nothing, and the caption above the table still reads "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" until the round trip completes. The picker is built this way on purpose — the partial that renders it says "no client JS anywhere" and its search button is a form submit told apart from Save and continue only by its action value (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:8-12, :86-91). A trader who mistypes a farm name gets a page load, an empty table and the "no matches" line rather than a list that shrinks and grows under their hands.

DR1 filters the table on every keystroke. Every matching address for the role is already on the page, each row carrying the text it is matched against, and the count above the table is a live figure that is rewritten as rows are hidden — "Showing 9 out of 9 results" becomes "Showing 2 out of 9 results" while the trader is still typing (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:70-96). The magnifying-glass button beside the box re-runs the same filter and returns focus to the box; there is no submit and no reload, and nothing but the browser's own scroll position moves.

Make the picker's search narrow the list as the trader types, and update the result count with it, without a page load. The frontend already computes the same match — its search runs over name and every address line — so the change is a progressive enhancement over the markup that is there rather than a new matching rule, with the existing Search button kept as the no-JavaScript path. This does not ask for DR1's pagination behaviour. DR1 renders every matching address at once and has no pager, but its address book holds nine records against the frontend's thirteen, so the capture cannot show what DR1 would do with a book big enough to need one; the frontend's pager should stay, and live filtering should narrow the current page rather than replace paging.

increments.title: DR1 lets the user import any of twenty-one commodities; the frontend offers five, so sheep, pigs, poultry, rabbits, bees, reptiles and the rest cannot be notified at all.
increments.detail:
The commodity page offers five commodities and eight species in total: Cow (0102) with Bison bison, Bos spp., Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis; Horse (0101) with Equus caballus; Cat (01061900) with Felis catus; Dog (01061900) with Canis lupus familiaris; Fish (0301) with Salmo salar. The list is not filtered or paged, so that is the whole catalogue a user can reach. It is a hard-coded module — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:1-26 — and its own comment says the non-cow commodities carry "one representative species each". A user importing sheep, pigs, goats, poultry, rabbits, camels, parrots, reptiles, bees or ferrets has no option to choose.

DR1 carries twenty-one commodities — Bees, Camel, Cat, Cattle, Chicken, Dog, Duck, Ferret, Goat, Goose, Guinea fowl, Horse, Ornamental fish, Ostrich, Other live mammals, Parrot, Pig, Rabbit, Reptile, Sheep and Turkey — with their species beneath them (app/data/commodities.js:9-291). Cattle alone carries eleven species against the frontend's four, Horse three against one, Ornamental fish three against one, and "Other live mammals" more than a hundred. Each commodity also carries the per-commodity rules that hang off it: which identifiers it needs, whether it asks for a package count, and whether it asks the unweaned question.

Widen the commodity catalogue to DR1's twenty-one commodities and their species. This replaces as well as adds: DR1 has no farmed-fish commodity at all, so the frontend's Fish (0301) with Salmo salar has no DR1 counterpart and gives way to Ornamental fish (030111) with Cichlidae, Cyprinidae and Poeciliidae. The catalogue is a local data module on both sides, so this is a data change rather than an integration, but every commodity carries rules with it, and in the frontend those rules are eight allow-lists keyed by commodity name in the same module — package count, passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, permanent address, unweaned animals and CPH, at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:50-119. Each new commodity needs an entry in every list that applies to it, and three of those entries are why other parts of this comparison raised no finding of their own and deferred to this one. First, permanent address: DR1 requires a permanent address for Ferret as well as for cat and dog, so the permanent-address list has to gain Ferret when Ferret lands. Second, ear tag: DR1 gives Pig, Sheep and Goat an ear tag, where the frontend's ear-tag list is Cow alone. Third, CPH: DR1 decides the CPH question from the commodity code and asks it for every code except horses and the 01061900 group of cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals, so Pig (0103), Sheep, Goat and most of the new commodities all need a CPH number where the frontend's CPH list is Cow alone. Do not port DR1's per-commodity certification-purpose lists; they are unused data on the requirements side, where the certification question is fed by one flat sixteen-option list that does not vary by commodity. Confirm before starting that the notification payload mapping accepts the new commodity codes; if it does not, this becomes backend work first.

increments.title: DR1 asks the user to search for a commodity by common name, code or Latin name; the frontend prints the whole catalogue as a static checkbox list with no search control at all.
increments.detail:
Under the heading "What are you importing?" the user meets the entire commodity catalogue at once: five checkbox fieldsets, legended Cow (0102), Horse (0101), Cat (01061900), Dog (01061900) and Fish (0301), holding eight species between them, every one of them rendered on arrival. There is no text box, no search button, no filter and no result count. The template loops over every group the commodity service returns and prints it, in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:20-29. The corpus names this screen fe-commodity-search and the page does not search.

The same page opens on an empty labelled search box — the label is "Search for a commodity", the hint is "You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus)", and a magnifying-glass button sits inside the field (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:48-116). Nothing else is on the page until the user types. A search returns a grouped result list rendered beneath the input: a commodity header row carrying the name and code with the matched text emphasised, then one checkbox per matching species under it, and the number of matches is announced through a polite live region — the captured results state shows a "cattle" search returning a Cattle (0102) header and eleven species, with "11 results available" in the status region.

Replace the static grouped checkbox list with a search control: a labelled input named commoditySearch carrying DR1's hint, a search button, results grouped under a commodity header row with the matched substring emphasised, and a polite live region announcing the number of matches. The list must become the result of searching rather than the whole catalogue printed on arrival — the search sits in place of the current fieldsets, not above them. Nothing blocks this, but it is the natural home for two findings that travel with it: the wider catalogue the search would be searching (commodities--commodity-catalogue) and the running selection summary a transient result list needs (commodities--search-selection-summary).

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any text input, search box or filter control on the frontend's commodity page in any state. Its rendered DOM holds no input element other than the CSRF token and the eight species checkboxes, and the list is not paged or filtered, so no other state can introduce one.

increments.title: DR1 asks whether the consignment contains unweaned animals only when it holds cattle or pigs; the frontend also asks it for a horse-only consignment.

The unweaned question is rendered when the notification's scope holds containsUnweanedAnimals (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/additional-details/template.njk:26-39), and the obligation puts it in scope when any commodity line's commodity is on an allow-list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/aggregates.js:46-55). That allow-list is Cow and Horse, the only two of the frontend's five commodities on it. DR1 additionally suppresses the question outright when every selected commodity is 01061900, which covers cat, dog and ferret. So on DR1 a horse-only consignment reaches this page, is asked what the animals are certified for, and is not asked the unweaned question at all.

Before making the change, settle the contradiction: the frontend's obligation names its source as the V4 data fields and lists equines, cattle, pigs, sheep and goats, while DR1 records unweaned options against cattle and pig alone. One of the two is out of date and the designer has to say which.

increments.title: The frontend has an amend journey for a submitted notification, with its own "Cancel this amendment?" page; DR1 tells the user a submitted notification can be changed from the dashboard but gives them no control that does it.
increments.detail:
A submitted notification's dashboard row carries View, Amend, Copy as new and Delete (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:29-42). Pressing Amend reopens the notification for editing and moves it to an Amending state, tagged yellow. While amending, the row gains a "Cancel amendment" action, and that opens a page headed "Cancel this amendment?" which explains "Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored." and offers "Yes, cancel amendment" or "No, return to notification" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cancel-amend/copy/copy.en.js:1-6). So the frontend defines a whole editing mode with an entry, a distinct status and an escape hatch.

DR1's submission confirmation page has a section headed "How to view or amend this notification" that tells the user "You can view or change this notification from your dashboard." But the dashboard it sends them to offers each row only "Copy as new" and "View" (app/views/dashboard.html:258-262). There is no amend control, no amending state — the status vocabulary runs Draft, Submitted, In progress, Approved, Action required, Rejected, Complete with no editing state among them — and no cancellation. The one thing DR1 does define is where View goes: on a notification just submitted it opens the review page read-only rather than the dead "#" the seeded rows use.

DR1 contradicts itself here, which is why this cannot be resolved from the evidence: it promises in prose that a submitted notification can be changed from the dashboard and then provides no way to do it. A designer has to settle whether amending is in scope, and if it is, DR1 needs four things the frontend has already guessed at — the control that starts an amendment, what the notification's status reads while it is being amended, what the authority sees in the meantime, and what abandoning an amendment does to the version already submitted. Until then the frontend's amend journey cannot be called either right or wrong. If amending turns out to be out of scope, the sentence on the submission page is the thing that changes, not the dashboard.

increments.title: The frontend lets a notification be deleted from the dashboard — a submitted one as readily as a draft — and DR1 defines no delete anywhere.
increments.detail:
Every row on the frontend dashboard carries a Delete link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-68). It opens a page of its own headed "Delete this notification?" whose only body text is "This cannot be undone.", offering a red "Yes, delete notification" button and a "No, return to dashboard" button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/delete-notification/copy/copy.en.js:1-6). The action is not limited to drafts: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/delete-notification/controller.js:19-22 admits draft, submitted and amending notifications alike, so a notification the authority has already received can be removed from the user's dashboard with one confirmation and no explanation of what that means. Underneath, the record is soft-deleted rather than destroyed, which the page's "This cannot be undone." does not tell the user.

DR1's dashboard row offers two actions and neither is delete: "Copy as new" and "View" (app/views/dashboard.html:258-262). No DR1 root view, route or link mentions deleting a notification, and the only delete-notification page in the prototype checkout sits under the design-release-2 and design-release-2.1 subtrees, which are later releases and not on trial here. DR1 is not squeamish about deletion in general: its address book gives a saved address a red Delete button on its own view page (app/views/address-book-view.html:43-46). It simply never applies the idea to a notification.

This is a capability the implementation has and the signed-off design does not describe, so there is nothing to bring the frontend into line with and nothing here for a developer to pick up yet. It needs a designer's ruling, and the ruling has to answer three things rather than one: whether a user may delete a notification at all; if so, whether that includes one already submitted to the authority or drafts only; and what the confirmation should say, because "This cannot be undone." is both the whole of the current explanation and not quite true of a soft delete. Until that is answered the finding cannot be settled either way. Nothing in the evidence can settle it — DR1's silence is equally consistent with delete being out of scope and with it having been overlooked.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a delete action, a delete confirmation, or any mention of removing a notification reachable from a DR1 session — a control on a root view, or a route that renders rather than redirects when the session is not a design-release-2 one.

Until that is answered the finding cannot be settled either way. Nothing in the evidence can settle it — DR1's silence is equally consistent with delete being out of scope and with it having been overlooked.
finding.correction: The finding survives and the slots are left alone, but its falsifier is written loosely enough to fire on something that does not falsify it, which would cost the next reader an hour. It says any DR1 "route" mentioning deletion would settle it, and there is one: app/routes.js:10044 mounts GET /notifications/delete on the prototype's root router, with a POST beside it at :10048. Neither is reachable from DR1. renderDeleteNotificationPage (app/routes.js:5607-5613) redirects straight back to the dashboard unless isDesignRelease2SessionData(req.session.data), and the dashboard rows only carry a deleteHref when that same predicate is true (app/routes.js:6621-6623 and :6682-6684), so a DR1 session is never given the link and would be bounced if it typed the path. The falsifier has been narrowed to say that. One point in the finding's own reasoning is worth naming plainly, because it separates this finding from its sibling: DR1 does not contradict itself about delete the way it does about amend. It is simply silent, and the finding says so. That silence is why disputed is the honest band — DR1's address book proves the service is willing to delete things (app/views/address-book-view.html:43-46 gives a saved address a govuk-button--warning Delete), so the omission on notifications reads as a decision nobody wrote down rather than an oversight anyone can settle from the evidence.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a delete action, a delete confirmation, or any mention of removing a notification reachable from a DR1 session — a control on a root view, or a route that renders rather than redirects when the session is not a design-release-2 one.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both screenshots, and followed the delete through the source on both sides. The claim this slice rests on — that the frontend's delete is not limited to drafts — holds and I checked it twice: delete-notification/controller.js:19-22 defines deletable as DRAFT or SUBMITTED or AMEND, and the POST handler re-checks the same predicate at :44 before calling softDeleteJourney, so there is no second gate that quietly excludes a submitted notification. dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:25-28 builds one deleteAction and attaches it to all three status branches at :40, :50 and :64. The confirmation page is verbatim as described: fe-delete-notification.html:115 "Delete this notification?", :116 "This cannot be undone.", :121-122 a govuk-button--warning "Yes, delete notification", :125 "No, return to dashboard". The soft-delete claim holds on both adapters — real posts to a /soft-delete endpoint (services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/transition.js:44-49) and the stub sets the record to DELETED and filters it out of the list (services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:22-24) — so the record survives a confirmation that says it cannot be undone. On the DR1 side, dr1-dashboard.html:707-709 and dr1-dashboard-after-submission.html:707-709 offer Copy as new and View and nothing else. Ran the falsifier: see correction — it fires on the letter and not on the substance. Band disputed upheld.

relatedTo.why: the same designer's ruling covers both — what a user may do to a notification the authority has already received

increments.title: DR1 tracks a notification through seven statuses including "Submitted action required", "Approved" and "Rejected"; the frontend has only Draft, Submitted, Amending and Deleted.
increments.detail:
A frontend notification row shows one of four tags: Draft (blue), Submitted (green), Amending (yellow) or Deleted (grey) — src/server/app/shared/kit.js:34-51 and src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:47-52. The captured row is tagged Draft. Nothing the authority does to a notification after it is received can change the tag: once submitted it reads "Submitted" for ever, and the user has no way to learn from the dashboard that something is wrong with it.

DR1's dashboard tags two of its four notifications "Submitted action required" in orange and two "Submitted" in green (app/views/dashboard.html:265-292). Its status filter names the full vocabulary: Draft, Submitted, In progress, Approved, Action required, Rejected, Complete. So a DR1 notification moves through a lifecycle owned by the authority, and the dashboard is where the user finds out about it — an orange "Submitted action required" tag is the service telling the user to come back and do something.

The notification record needs a status that the authority can set after submission, and the dashboard needs to render it. That is a backend change first: the status today is a frontend-side lifecycle (draft, submitted, amending, deleted) with no channel for a decision coming back. Once the status arrives, map each of the seven to a tag colour and add the matching filter option. Whether "Action required" and "Submitted action required" are one status or two is worth settling before building — DR1 uses the first in its filter and the second on its cards.

increments.title: DR1 lists the user's own notifications however long ago they were made; the frontend dashboard is scoped to the browser session against the stub and to nothing at all against the real backend.
increments.detail:
The frontend's empty dashboard says so itself: "You have not started any notifications in this session." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:56, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:157-159). The dashboard asks for a list of the journey ids this session happens to remember, not a list of the user's notifications: src/server/app/engine/journey.js:92-119 reads the ids out of the session store and passes them to the list query as a filter, and they live there for the life of the session (src/server/app/services/persistence/session/real.js:6-24). Which notifications that actually produces depends on which store is behind it, and neither answer is the user's own. Against the stub, the filter is applied (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:15-23), so a user who signs out, comes back tomorrow, or opens the service on a second device meets an empty dashboard whatever they created or submitted before — that is the captured behaviour. Against the real backend the filter is silently dropped: the list read sends only page, sort and reference number (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:24-39), so the dashboard shows every notification the service holds, including other people's.

DR1 heads the list "My notifications" and shows four notifications belonging to the user, three of them submitted days earlier with an arrival date in the future and a status the authority has since set (app/views/dashboard.html:80-294). Two of the four read "Submitted action required", a state that can only be reached after the user has gone away and come back. DR1's status filter offers Approved, Rejected and Complete on the same terms, so the list is required to survive the session that created it.

The dashboard has to list the notifications belonging to the signed-in user or their organisation — not the ones this browser session happens to remember, and not everything the service holds. That means the list read stops filtering on session-held journey ids and asks the backend for the caller's notifications instead, which needs the list endpoint to support an owner-scoped query and the records to carry an owner. Do this before the status work and the filter work: filtering a session's handful of drafts by status or arrival date has little to filter. The real adapter dropping the session filter is a separate defect from the parity gap and wants raising on its own, but the fix here supersedes it — an owner-scoped read is what both need.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the frontend's list read scoped to the signed-in user or their organisation: an owner or organisation parameter in the query the real adapter sends to the notifications endpoint, rather than page, sort and reference number alone.

finding.correction: The finding is right that the dashboard is not the user's, and the correction makes it worse rather than better. What was claimed: "The list is built from the journey ids held in the session cookie and nothing else", and that a user returning tomorrow "meets an empty dashboard". What is true: that is the stub adapter's behaviour, and it is what the capture shows — the header names stub.user@example.com and services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:15-23 applies the journeyIds filter. The real adapter ignores the filter entirely. engine/journey.js:113-119 passes journeyIds into records.list, and services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:24-39 destructures page, sort, referenceNumber and organisationId and never reads journeyIds, building the query as page, sort and an optional referenceNumber only. So against the real backend the falsifier as written would have fired — a second browser would show the notification — while leaving the finding's substance untouched, because it would show every other trader's notifications too. Two smaller imprecisions, corrected in the slot: the ids are not in the cookie but in the yar server-side store the cookie keys (common/helpers/session-cache/session-cache.js:10-27), which is why they also expire on a TTL; and organisationId at engine/journey.js:101 scopes the address-book lookup used to resolve party names, not the notification list, so it is not a second filter. increments.title: DR1 offers three ways to sort the dashboard — newest first, oldest first, arrival date — with nothing chosen to begin with; the frontend offers four combined date-and-direction options and starts already sorted by arrival, newest first.
increments.detail:
The frontend's sort control is labelled "Sort by" and offers four options — "Arrival (newest to oldest)", "Arrival (oldest to newest)", "Date created (newest to oldest)" and "Date created (oldest to newest)" — with the first of them already selected on arrival at the page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:27-36, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:70-77). There is no unsorted starting state and no option that names a date without also naming a direction.

DR1's control is labelled "Sort by:" and offers "Select one", "Newest first", "Oldest first" and "Arrival date", with "Select one" chosen (app/views/dashboard.html:240-250). Two of its three real options say only which end of the list comes first and leave the date they sort on unstated, and the third names arrival without a direction.

Bring the option set into line with DR1: a "Select one" placeholder as the starting state, then "Newest first", "Oldest first" and "Arrival date". Two things have to be settled before the wording can be applied, and they are the reason this is worth writing down rather than treating as a copy tweak — which date DR1's "Newest first" and "Oldest first" order on, and which direction its "Arrival date" runs in. Neither is stated anywhere in DR1, so a designer answers them and the frontend then maps the four values it already supports onto the three DR1 asks for. This finding is about the options offered and how they read. Whether the list re-sorts on choosing or on pressing a button is deliberately left out: DR1's select sits in a form with no submit control of its own, and that is as likely to be the Prototype Kit as a design decision.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a "Newest first" or "Oldest first" option, or an unselected placeholder, in the frontend dashboard's sort control.

increments.title: Three of the frontend's add-a-document error messages are worded differently from the messages DR1 states, including telling the trader to "Select a file to upload" where DR1 says "Upload a document".
increments.detail:
The four messages the add form can produce are held in one block (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:63-81). One matches DR1 word for word — "Enter a document reference". Three do not: the missing date reads "Enter the date of issue", the missing file reads "Select a file to upload", and an unparseable date reads "Enter a real date of issue". No captured frontend state shows any of them; they are read from the copy file, and the validators that fire them are in the same feature (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/form/errors.js:21-41).

DR1's blank-form state, captured at dr1-upload-documents-error, shows the same three fields failing with "Enter a document reference", "Enter a date of issue" and "Upload a document", each linked from the summary to its field; the invalid-date message is "Enter a real date" (app/routes.js:9101-9155). Align the three strings in the English and Welsh copy files: "Enter a date of issue", "Upload a document", "Enter a real date". Nothing else moves — the same validators fire in the same order against the same fields. One of the three is worth a designer's eye rather than a blind copy: the frontend's "Enter a real date of issue" names the field and DR1's "Enter a real date" does not, which is the only case here where the frontend's wording is the more specific of the two.

increments.title: DR1 offers a drop zone that names the chosen file back to the trader; the frontend offers the browser's own file button and nothing else.
increments.detail:
The file question renders govukFileUpload with no options beyond a label, a hint and an accept list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:51-58), so what the trader meets is whatever the browser draws for a bare file input — in the capture, a "Choose File" button and the words "No file chosen" in the browser's own styling, which varies by browser and is not announced when it changes. There is no drop target and no application-owned statement of which file is currently attached.

DR1 draws a dashed drop target holding a status line, a "Choose file" button and the words "or drop file" (app/views/upload-documents.html:171-181). The status line reads "No file chosen" until a file is picked and then shows its name — dr1-upload-documents-file-chosen captures it reading "itahc-certificate.pdf" — and it is an aria-live region, so the change is announced rather than only drawn. When the attachment is in error the target itself is outlined in red alongside the message.

Pass javascript: true to the existing govukFileUpload call. The service is already on govuk-frontend 6.3.0, whose file upload component provides exactly this behaviour and exactly these strings — the component's own default button text is "Choose file" and its default drop instruction is "or drop file", the two strings DR1 renders — so DR1 is asking for the component's enhanced mode, not for anything bespoke. Check that the component's JavaScript is included in the documents bundle, since the page ships its own entry point, and that the no-JavaScript fallback still renders the plain input.

increments.title: DR1 saves — or refuses to leave — a part-filled add-a-document form when the trader presses Save and continue; the frontend throws the answers away without a word.
increments.detail:
Continue never looks at the add-a-document form. The post handler branches on the action: 'add' validates and saves, a remove action removes, and everything else falls through to a check on whether any already-saved document is still being scanned and then a redirect to the next page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:255-279). A trader who types a reference, picks a date, chooses a file and then presses Continue instead of "Save and add another" loses all three silently — no error, no saved record, and no warning that the page they are leaving is now empty. No captured frontend state shows this; it is read from the handler.

DR1 treats Save and continue as a save. Uploads stay optional, but once a document type has been chosen the whole add form is validated before the trader can leave, and if it passes the document is added on the way out (app/routes.js:10174-10193, whose own comment states the rule as "uploads are optional, but once a document type is chosen all document fields must be completed before continuing"). dr1-upload-documents-continue-error captures the refusal: three errors — "Enter a document reference", "Enter a date of issue", "Upload a document" — on a form where only the document type had been filled in and no document had been saved.

On Continue, look at the add-a-document form before redirecting. If any of its fields carries an answer, run the same validation the Add action runs and either save the document or re-render with the errors; if every field is empty, continue as now. DR1 uses the document type as the trigger for this, and the frontend has no such field today, so the trigger has to be "any field answered" until the type select lands. Scope this to Continue only: the two exit actions beside it discard the part-filled form as well, but so does DR1's own "Save and return to overview", so changing them would move the frontend away from DR1 rather than towards it.

FALSIFIED BY: Filling the frontend's add-a-document form, pressing Continue, and finding either the document saved or an error shown.

increments.title: DR1 asks the trader to choose a document type from a thirteen-option list; the frontend never asks and guesses the type from the uploaded file's name.
increments.detail:
The add-a-document form asks three questions — Document reference, Date of issue and Upload a file — and carries no document-type control of any kind (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:31-58). The type is guessed after the fact from the file name: the words in the name, extension stripped and separators flattened, are matched against the document-type enum and anything that does not match becomes 'OTHER' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/derive-document-type.js:19-23). The controller stamps that guess onto the record it saves (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:108-112). So a certificate saved as scan1.pdf is filed as Other, the trader is never asked, never shown the guess before it is made, and cannot correct it — the added-documents table prints the derived label with no change link beside it.

DR1 puts a Document type select between Document reference and Date of issue, starting on "Select one" and offering thirteen types: Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC), Veterinary health certificate, Air waybill, Import permit, Letter of authority (Directive 2008/61/EC), Commercial invoice, Sea waybill, Rail waybill, Bill of lading, Catch certificate, Laboratory sampling results for aflatoxin (Reg 2019/1793), Journey log, Other (app/views/upload-documents.html:116-129). It is mandatory: pressing "Save and add another" with the form blank produces four errors, one of which is "Select a document type" linked to the select, and the document is not saved.

Add a mandatory Document type select to the add-a-document form, between Document reference and Date of issue, with DR1's thirteen options and a "Select one" placeholder, and a "Select a document type" error when it is left unset. The obligation the answer belongs to already exists and is already marked mandatory (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:30-35), so the model already expects a real answer here and is currently being fed a guess. Once the question is asked, derive-document-type.js and its test become dead and should be deleted rather than kept as a default — a wrong guess a trader cannot see is worse than no guess. The saved record already carries the field, so nothing downstream changes shape.

increments.title: DR1 accepts document files up to 50MB; the frontend refuses anything over 10 MB.
increments.detail:
The file question's hint reads "Your file must be:" over the bullet "smaller than 10 MB", and the same 10 MB is enforced twice — in the browser, from the data-max-file-size attribute on the form, and on the server, where an oversize upload is answered with "The selected file must be smaller than 10 MB" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-52). The constant is deliberate rather than arbitrary: the comment above it records that 10 MB decimal was chosen to sit clear of the CDP nginx ingress cap of 10 MiB.

DR1's file requirements list opens with "files that are smaller than 50MB" (app/views/upload-documents.html:165-170) — five times the frontend's ceiling, and the first thing the trader reads about their file.

Raise the accepted file size to 50MB. It is one frontend constant: MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB in upload-config.js feeds the hint bullet, the data-max-file-size attribute the browser check reads, the hapi route's payload maxBytes, the server-side size check and the oversize error's own wording, so all five move together when the number does. Nothing has to land first — the backend already accepts a file this size, and takes its per-upload ceiling from whatever the frontend sends it. The one thing to settle before the copy changes is the platform: a comment beside the constant records a CDP nginx ingress cap of 10 MiB, and if that cap is real and unchanged a 50MB file will be refused at the edge before the application sees it. Confirm the ingress limit with the platform team and raise it in the same piece of work, because a hint promising 50MB over an ingress that refuses it is worse than the honest 10 MB.

FALSIFIED BY: Uploading a file between 10 MB and 50MB through the frontend and having it accepted.

increments.title: DR1 tells the trader that JPG files are allowed and that ZIP files are not; the frontend's file requirements say neither.
increments.detail:
The file requirements hint has two bullets: a size and "a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS or XLSX". JPG is missing from that sentence even though the field accepts it — the list is built by de-duplicating the allowed types on MIME type, and .jpg shares image/jpeg with .jpeg, so it is dropped from the label while staying in the input's accept attribute and in the server-side check (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:3-38). Nothing says ZIP is refused; a trader who picks one learns it only after submitting, from "The selected file must be a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS or XLSX".

DR1's list has four bullets, two of which the frontend has no counterpart for: "PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX" names JPG explicitly, and "ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons" states the prohibition and the reason before the trader chooses a file (app/views/upload-documents.html:165-170).

Name JPG in the allowed-types sentence and add DR1's ZIP line to the file requirements list. The types sentence is generated rather than written, so the de-duplication that hides .jpg has to go — build the label from the extensions, not from the MIME types, or the two files that share image/jpeg will keep collapsing to one. The ZIP line is static copy for both languages. Neither changes what the field accepts.

increments.title: DR1 opens the upload-documents page with guidance on which documents are needed, including a table of extra documents by consignment type; the frontend page has none of it.
increments.detail:
The page runs from the heading straight into the first question: h1 "Upload documents", then the Document reference input (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:16-39). Nothing tells the trader which documents this page is for, that an ITAHC is expected where the consignment needs one, that documents can be added later, that they must be in English, that every page must be uploaded, or that documents should be in before the consignment reaches the port. All of it is static copy, so it lands in the feature's copy files with a Welsh counterpart; the three consignment rows are the only part that carries policy and should be confirmed as current before they are typed in. increments.title: DR1 lets a trader attach fifteen documents and says so up front; the frontend stops at ten and only mentions a limit once the eleventh is refused.
increments.detail:
The documents collection is capped at ten entries (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:19-28). An eleventh attempt is refused before any validation runs, with the summary error "You can add a maximum of 10 documents" pointing at the added-documents table (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:92-100). Nothing on the page warns of the cap beforehand: the file requirements hint lists only a size and a set of file types (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:43-49). No captured frontend state shows the refusal — both frontend captures hold zero or one document.

DR1's ceiling is fifteen and the trader is told before they start: "up to a maximum of 15 files" is the third bullet in the file requirements list. Reaching it is captured at dr1-upload-documents-limit-error — fifteen rows in the table and a single error, "You can upload a maximum of 15 files", shown both in the summary and against the Attachment field, with the rest of the form's validation skipped (app/views/upload-documents.html:165-170).

Raise maxEntries from 10 to 15, restate the error as "You can upload a maximum of 15 files", and add the ceiling to the file requirements bullets so the trader meets it before they hit it. Attaching the error to the Attachment field rather than to the table, as DR1 does, is part of the same change. Nothing outside the frontend holds a competing cap, so the three edits are the whole of the work.

FALSIFIED BY: Adding an eleventh document through the frontend and having it saved.

It does not. That string occurs in exactly two places in the frontend and nowhere else: the obligation itself (obligations/sections/documents.js:26, declared on the same object as maxEntries: 10) and an obligation-evaluator test. A search of trade-imports-animals-backend src/main returns no occurrence of the code, of tooMany, or of any accompanying-document count limit at all. The sentence has been struck and replaced; the band was already frontend-work and is now unqualified rather than hedged.

finding.verification: Read both sides. The frontend cap is maxEntries: 10 at obligations/sections/documents.js:25 inside the cited 19-28, and the refusal at controller.js:96-100 does precede documentAddErrors at :101, so "refused before any validation runs" is exact; the message is built as `You can add a maximum of ${max} documents` (copy.en.js:73) and anchored to the added-documents table (form/errors.js:52-56), and neither frontend capture's hint mentions a count. DR1's side is captured rather than inferred: dr1-upload-documents-limit-error holds fifteen table rows and exactly one error, "You can upload a maximum of 15 files", linked to #attachment, with no other field in error — confirming the early return that skips the rest of validation at routes.js:9106-9113, and "up to a maximum of 15 files" is the third requirements bullet in the DOM. increments.title: The frontend refuses to let a trader continue while any document is still being scanned, and offers a manual refresh link; DR1 lets them continue and finishes the check by itself.
increments.detail:
Pressing Continue while any document's scan is unsettled re-renders the page with the summary error "You cannot continue until all documents have been scanned or removed" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/scan/summary-errors.js:21-24, fired from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:272-277); a document whose scan came back rejected is named instead, file by file. While a scan is pending the page also offers a "Refresh virus scan status" link for traders without JavaScript, and a hidden timeout line reading "Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:82-87). Neither captured frontend state is mid-scan, so this is read from source.

DR1's continue path has no scan check at all: it validates the add form when a document type has been chosen, saves, and moves on regardless of what any row's tag says (app/routes.js:10174-10193). dr1-upload-documents-populated-scanning shows a document tagged "Scanning for virus" with Save and continue live beside it and no error, and dr1-upload-documents-limit-error shows fifteen rows all mid-scan on a page whose only complaint is the file count. There is no refresh control anywhere; the tag settles on its own.

What is not in doubt is the difference: a frontend trader is held on the page until every scan settles, a DR1 trader is not. What cannot be settled from the evidence is whether DR1 is stating a requirement or simply not modelling one. Its virus check is a fiction — a browser-side timer posts to a stub endpoint after a fixed delay and flips the row to passed, and no path in the prototype can ever produce a failed check (app/routes.js:9026 and 10124-10132) — so a design that never has a failure to catch would not need a gate whether or not the real service does. Settle it with a designer: if a real submission must not carry an unscanned or infected attachment, the frontend's gate is right and DR1 is silent rather than contrary, and this finding should be struck. If a trader is meant to be able to continue and be told later, the gate and the refresh link both come out. One fact sharpens the question for whoever settles it: the frontend's gate is not a rule about submission, it is a rule about one button. It is skipped whenever the trader leaves by "Save and return to hub", so an unsettled scan can already be walked past today — the gate delays the trader on this page rather than keeping an unscanned attachment out of a notification. If the intent is the latter, the check belongs on the submission path, not on Continue.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any statement in DR1 — on the page, in the hub, or on the check-answers page — that a notification may be submitted while a document is still being scanned, or that it may not.

finding.verification: The band and the reasoning behind it both hold, and I tried to break the reasoning rather than read it. DR1's virus status takes exactly two values in the whole prototype: documents are created with virusStatus: 'uploading' (routes.js:9167) and the only writer anywhere is markUploadedDocumentVirusCheckPassed, which sets 'passed' and nothing else (:9172-9176); it is reached only from the stub endpoint at :10124-10132, driven by a browser timer of VIRUS_CHECK_DELAY_MS = 2500 (:9026, and app/assets/javascripts/upload-documents-virus-check.js:5,19,44). A grep for virusStatus across routes.js returns no third state and no failure path, so the author's premise — that DR1 has no failure to catch and its silence may be prototype fidelity rather than a requirement — is sound, and disputed is the honest band. The frontend half checks out too: settlingSummaryErrors returns the cannotContinue message only when nothing is REJECTED and rejectedErrors names files individually otherwise (scan/summary-errors.js:11-24, prepended on every render at view-model/render.js:30-34), fired from controller.js:273-277; the "for traders without JavaScript" characterisation of the refresh link is right, since the client hides #js-refresh-fallback as soon as polling starts (client/scan-status/poll.js:57-70). increments.title: The frontend tags a scanned document "Safe" and a pending one "Checking"; DR1 tags them "Check completed" and "Scanning for virus", and says out loud which document each tag belongs to.
increments.detail:
The Status column holds a bare tag and nothing else. The captured row shows a green "Safe"; the other three states the page can render are "Checking" (blue), "Virus found" (red) and "Unknown" (grey), all four carried in the copy file and also handed to the client bundle so it can rewrite the cell as a scan settles (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:52-57, and the cell built at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/view-model/rows.js:39-44). Because the tag is the only content of the cell, a screen reader reaching it hears "Safe" with nothing to say what is safe.

DR1 uses two tags — green "Check completed" once the check has passed and blue "Scanning for virus" until then (app/views/upload-documents.html:213-224). Both captured: dr1-upload-documents-populated shows the completed tag, dr1-upload-documents-populated-scanning the same row mid-scan. Each cell also opens with a visually hidden sentence naming the record, "Virus check status for ITAHC-2026-0001", so the tag is never heard on its own.

Rename the two settled tags to "Check completed" and "Scanning for virus" in the English and Welsh copy, in the server-rendered cell and in the JSON the client bundle uses to rewrite it — they must change together or a page will flip wording as a scan finishes. Add the hidden "Virus check status for <document reference>" sentence ahead of the tag in the same cell. DR1 has no counterpart for the frontend's "Virus found" and "Unknown" tags because its virus check is simulated and can only pass, so those two keep their current wording and are not part of this change.

finding.verification: Checked all six tag strings character by character in the rendered DOM of both sides rather than in the page model, and opened the populated and scanning screenshots. The frontend's captured cell is `Safe` with no other content, and the data-scan-copy payload on #js-scan-status-announcer carries all four states verbatim — COMPLETE "Safe", PENDING "Checking", REJECTED "Virus found", UNKNOWN "Unknown" — matching copy.en.js:52-57 exactly and confirming the finding's point that the server-rendered cell and the client's rewrite copy must move together (view-model/fragments/status.js:7-29 builds both from the same object). increments.title: DR1's hub always shows the animal and package totals, reading zero when nothing has been added; the frontend hides the whole "Your commodities" panel until a commodity exists.
increments.detail:
On a notification with no commodity chosen the hub goes straight from the "Overview" heading to "1. About the consignment" — there is no "Your commodities" heading and no counter cards anywhere in the rendered page. The panel is behind a condition (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/template.njk:8-26) fed by a builder that returns nothing when the commodity collection is empty (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:142-146). Once a commodity line exists the panel appears, showing 0 animals and 0 packages until the quantities are filled in.

DR1's hub renders the "Your commodities" heading and both cards on every visit, and prints "0" when there is nothing to count (app/routes.js:5746-5747). The captured hub, with nothing answered at all, shows 0 Animals and 0 Packages/boxes above the task list.

Render the totals panel unconditionally, showing zero for both counts when there are no commodity lines. That is the condition in template.njk:8 and the null return in controller.js:142-146; the sum helpers already produce 0 for an empty list. The user-facing point is that the hub keeps the same shape from the first visit rather than growing a section part way through.

FALSIFIED BY: A frontend hub rendered with no commodity lines that still shows the "Your commodities" heading and the two counter cards.

increments.title: The frontend labels the documents task "Optional", telling a user they can skip it; DR1 lists it as a task to do and, if it is still undone at submission, tells the user to upload the health certificate before the import.
increments.detail:
The "5. Documents" section holds one row, "Uploaded documents", whose status is the bare word "Optional" rather than a tag. It never becomes "Completed" in the sense the other rows do, and because the review gate treats an optional row as satisfied (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15) a notification with no documents at all counts as ready to submit. The status comes from the documents collection carrying no minimum entry count (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:20-28).

DR1's hub shows "Upload documents" with the same "To do" tag as every other task and turns it green once a document exists (app/routes.js:5810-5819). Submitting without one is allowed but not silent: the submission confirmation lists "upload the health certificate and any other required documents" among the things that must be done before the import (app/routes.js:5674-5692).

Stop rendering the documents row as "Optional" and give it the same to-do and complete statuses as the other tasks. If submission is still to be allowed without documents, the outstanding upload has to be carried forward and shown to the user afterwards, which is where the substance of the difference lies — DR1 does not treat the health certificate as skippable, only as deferrable.

FALSIFIED BY: A frontend hub showing the documents row with a to-do or completed status tag rather than the word Optional.

increments.title: For a horses-for-temporary-entry notification the hub's Exit details row reads "Cannot start yet" and never changes, and the port of exit and exit date are asked nowhere on the way through — the only route to them is re-opening the reason page, which nothing signposts; DR1 asks both on the reason page itself.
increments.detail:
The hub shows an "Exit details" row under "1. About the consignment" with the hint "Where the consignment travels on to and when it leaves Great Britain", no link, and the status "Cannot start yet" — while every other row on the same page, including Additional commodity details and Uploaded documents, is a working link. That combination pins the state down. A row is offered only if the first page behind it passes, and the Exit details row's first page is Destination country (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-39, src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25). Pages later in the flow than Destination country are open, so the block is not a missing earlier answer; it is that the destination-country question is out of scope. The row is nonetheless shown rather than hidden, which only happens when at least one of its three questions is in scope (controller.js:93). The single reason for import that puts the port of exit and the exit date in scope while leaving the destination country out is "For horses authorised for temporary entry" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:61-116). Because the row's status is overwritten with "Cannot start yet" regardless of progress (controller.js:95), it would still read that way after the questions were answered, and because the opening run steps from the reason page past the exit questions to animal identification (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-39) a first-time user is never asked them on the way through. The one route left is to re-open "Main reason for importing" from the hub and press "Save and continue", which walks on to the port of exit and then the exit date. Nothing on the hub says so, and until those two answers exist the Check and submit row is blocked too, so a user who trusts the task list has no way of knowing what is holding the notification up.

DR1 has no exit-details task. The port of exit and the exit date are conditional reveals on the radios of the reason-for-import page (app/views/reason-for-import.html:47-62, whose four reveal blocks are supplied at app/routes.js:8778-8784), so choosing temporary admission of horses shows both questions immediately, on the page where the choice was made, and the hub's "Main reason for import" row covers them.

Make the row's availability follow the questions that are actually in scope rather than the first page listed against it — the row should open on Port of exit when Destination country does not apply — and stop overwriting a blocked row's status, so a completed exit-details row reads Completed. The wider structural difference, that DR1 asks all four reason-dependent questions inline on one page while the frontend splits them across four, is a separate change owned by the origin-and-reason slice; this finding is only about the hub row being shut and the questions behind it being unsignposted.

FALSIFIED BY: A frontend hub capture for a notification whose reason for import is horses authorised for temporary entry in which the Exit details row is a link, or in which it reads Completed after the port of exit and exit date have been given.

The row is declared without the conditional flag its neighbours use (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45), and only a conditional row is dropped when nothing it covers applies (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:93 and :116-118). DR1 adds "Identification details" to the task list only when at least one selected species has identifier fields (app/routes.js:5778-5782, testing the rule at app/routes.js:1489-1493). The captured DR1 hub, with no species chosen, has no identification row: its second section holds Commodity details and Additional details and nothing else.

Drop the identification row from the hub when no commodity line needs identifiers, the way the transit-countries row already drops. Two things have to move together: the row needs the conditional flag, and its status has to resolve to not-applicable in that case — the row's part is a facet of the commodityLines collection and a facet is keyed on its parent collection, so the flag on its own will not hide it while commodityLines is in scope. Without the change a user importing a species with no identifier requirement is shown a task that can never be completed, and a user who has chosen nothing yet is shown a task about animals they have not named.

increments.title: DR1 lets a user start any task on the hub from the first visit; the frontend greys nine of its eleven rows out as "Cannot start yet" until a country of origin and a commodity have been answered.
increments.detail:
On a notification where only the country of origin has been given, nine of the eleven hub rows carry no link and read "Cannot start yet" — Main reason for importing, Additional commodity details, Animal identification details, Arrival details, Transporter, Roles and addresses, Contact address, Uploaded documents and Check and submit. Only "Where is this consignment coming from?" and "What are you importing?" can be opened. The whole task list is held behind two answers: the country of origin and a commodity selection, the two obligations enforced at continue in src/server/app/bridge/obligation-source.js:31-34. A row is offered only when the first page behind it clears that check (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:103-123); otherwise the row is rendered without a link and its real status is replaced by "Cannot start yet" (:95).

Every row of DR1's task list is a link on every visit, whatever has been answered. The hub view model gives each of the twelve items a fixed href and one of exactly two statuses, "To do" or "Complete" (app/routes.js:5749-5841), so a user who has just created a notification can go straight to Transport details or Upload documents if that is what they have to hand.

Stop withholding hub rows. Render every task row as a link and let its status describe progress instead of permission, which means dropping the gate consulted in controller.js:120 and the "Cannot start yet" substitution at :95, and letting each page cope with being opened before its neighbours. The frontend's "cannot start" state is not the same thing as a page being unreachable: the questions behind the blocked rows are still asked, because a new notification is walked forward through origin, commodity search, commodity details, reason for import, animal identification and additional details before it ever lands on the hub (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-39), and once a commodity exists every answer row unblocks — the fe-hub capture, taken one answer later, shows ten of the eleven rows startable, the exception being Check and submit, which stays shut until the rest are done and is its own finding. What DR1 gives and the frontend does not is the choice of where to start.

increments.title: DR1 requires every identifier its commodity defines before an animal counts as identified; the frontend accepts any one of them
increments.detail:
Every identifier obligation is declared optional in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198, and the animal record above them requires only that one of the six is filled — `requires.anyOfIds` at :88-102, error code `obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired`. The save path matches: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/form/forms.js:22-23 counts a card as holding data when a single box is non-empty, and :124-135 raises the "at least one identifier" error only when the whole card is blank. So a cow entered with an ear tag and nothing else is a complete animal, and the passport and tattoo boxes can be left empty for good. fe-animal-identification-saved shows exactly that: a saved cattle animal whose whole summary reads "Ear tag: UK123456789012".

DR1 treats an animal as identified only when every field its commodity defines carries a value — `isAnimalIdentifierEntryComplete` in app/routes.js:1526-1532 tests `fields.every(...)`. A cattle animal saved with an ear tag but no passport does not advance the counter and does not appear in the saved list: the panel's active animal stays on the same index (:1590-1603) and the saved rows are filtered to complete entries only (:1621-1624). The user is pushed back to the same box until both are filled, and the identification task row stays Todo until every animal on every species has every field (:1534-1563).

Change the animal record's requirement from any-one-of to all-applicable: the six identifier obligations become mandatory where their commodity gate applies, and the `anyOfIds` requirement in identifiers.js:88-102 is replaced by per-field required errors. That means a required-field message per empty identifier rather than one "at least one identifier" message, so the error copy in the commodities copy file needs a per-field entry, and the empty-form guard in forms.js:124-135 is superseded. Check first whether the free-text fallback pair — Identification details and Animal description — should both become mandatory under the same rule, since DR1 has no commodity that pairs two free-text identifiers. Decide also which of DR1's two rules to mirror: its completeness rule is all-fields, but its submit gate is looser and demands identifiers only when more than one species is on the notification.

FALSIFIED BY: Saving a DR1 cattle animal with an ear tag and an empty passport and seeing it appear in the saved-animals list with the counter advancing to the next animal.

increments.title: DR1 skips the identification step entirely for a commodity it names no identifiers for; the frontend always asks two free-text questions instead
increments.detail:
A commodity that matches none of the four typed identifiers falls through to a pair of free-text boxes — "Identification details", hinted "Any other way this animal is identified, if it has no passport, tattoo or ear tag", and "Animal description". fe-animal-identification-fish shows exactly that for Fish (0301) — Salmo salar. The pair is declared as an inverse gate in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:174-198: they apply whenever the commodity is in none of the passport, tattoo, ear-tag or horse-name allow lists. Because the gate is a complement it can never be empty, so every commodity gets an identification card and the page can never be skipped.

DR1 attaches identifiers per commodity code and lets the list be empty — poultry, rabbit, camel, ostrich, parrot, reptile, bees and ornamental fish all carry `identifiers: []` in app/data/commodities.js. An empty list removes the species panel (app/routes.js:1571-1576 returns no panel state when there are no fields) and, if no selected species has any, removes the whole identification step from the journey (:1488-1492 and :1263-1265). DR1 has no free-text catch-all identifier anywhere. DR1 also has no 0301 commodity: its nearest entry is Ornamental fish at code 030111, with an empty identifier list.

Decide whether the free-text pair should exist at all. Under DR1 the answer is no: identifiers are per-commodity and an unlisted commodity is simply not asked. Removing them means the inverse-gate obligations in identifiers.js:174-198 go, the animal-record requirement narrows to the four typed identifiers, and the identification page needs a gate of its own so it disappears when no line on the notification has an identifier — today no such gate exists because the fallback guarantees one. This depends on the commodity catalogue: Fish is one of five commodities the frontend offers and DR1 does not, which is the commodities slice's business, and the identifier set DR1 would want for it has to come from a designer before this is scheduled.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a free-text identifier field, or any catch-all identifier not tied to a commodity code, in DR1's app/data/commodity-identifiers.js or on any DR1 identification panel.

increments.title: DR1 labels the identifier boxes "Passport" and "Ear tag"; the frontend calls them "Passport number" and "Ear tag number" and hangs worked examples under them that DR1 has none of
increments.detail:
The frontend labels the identifier boxes Passport number, Tattoo, Ear tag number and Horse name, and hangs a worked example under three of them — "For example, UK123456789" on the passport, "For example, AB1234" on the tattoo and "For example, UK123456789012" on the ear tag. fe-animal-identification shows all three cattle boxes with their hints; fe-animal-identification-horse shows Passport number and Horse name. The labels and hints are in the commodities copy file at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-72. The service already holds the shorter wording as a second list — Passport, Tattoo, Ear tag, Horse name at :48-55 — which it uses when it prints a saved animal's summary row, so the same identifier is called two different things in two places on the same page.

DR1 calls the same boxes Passport, Tattoo, Ear tag and Horse name, and gives none of them a hint. The dr1-animal-identification-details capture shows a cattle panel reading Ear tag then Passport with a bare input under each label and nothing else. The labels are the identifier definitions themselves in app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-20, and DR1 cannot show a hint on these boxes at all — the input that renders them (app/views/animal-identification-details.html:111-120) passes no hint argument, so even the two germinal-product codes whose data carries hint text render without one.

Rename the two identifier labels that differ, in the commodities copy file at copy.en.js:58-72 and its Welsh counterpart: "Passport number" becomes "Passport" and "Ear tag number" becomes "Ear tag". Tattoo and Horse name already match. Nothing else has to move — the saved-row labels at :48-55 already carry the shorter wording, so this ends the split rather than creating one, and the maximum-length error messages beside them read "Passport must be…" and "Ear tag must be…" already. The three worked examples are a second question and a designer's call rather than a copy fix: DR1 shows no example format on any identifier box, but dropping a format hint from a field whose format a user is unlikely to know is not obviously an improvement, so it is named here to be decided rather than rediscovered.

increments.title: DR1 asks for a microchip number when identifying horses, cats and dogs; the frontend never asks for one
increments.detail:
Identifying a horse offers two boxes, Passport number and Horse name, and nothing else — that is the whole entry form on fe-animal-identification-horse. Cats and dogs get Passport number and Tattoo. No screen in the service asks for a microchip number, and no field exists for one: the identifier set is fixed at six obligations in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198 — passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, identification details, description — with the labels in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-79. The only occurrence of the word microchip in the whole application is a test fixture typing "Microchip 900123" into the free-text identification-details box.

DR1 defines a microchip as an identifier on two commodity codes in app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-20 — 0101 (Horse), where the set is Microchip, Passport, Horse name, and 01061900 (Cat, Dog, Ferret, Other live mammals), where the set is Microchip, Passport, Tattoo. It is the first field in both sets, so on the identification page a horse, cat or dog line opens with a Microchip box above the others. No DR1 capture shows it: the corpus's only DR1 identification screenshot is a cattle line, and 0102 has no microchip.

Add a microchip identifier to the six-obligation identifier set: a new obligation in identifiers.js allow-listed to Horse, Cat and Dog, its label and hint in the commodities copy file, and its inclusion in the free-text fallback's inverse gate so a microchip commodity stops falling through to Identification details. DR1 places it first in the horse and cat/dog sets, so the field order changes too. Nothing blocks this in the frontend, but the value has to reach the notification payload, so check the identifier mapping in src/server/app/services/persistence/records/notification-mapper/ carries a sixth identifier before the field is added.
