increments.title: DR1 asks for each animal's permanent address on its own page among the consignment parties; the frontend asks it inside the identification entry form, one animal at a time
increments.detail:
The frontend does ask the question. It renders a "Permanent address" heading, the sentence "A permanent address is required for this animal." and a full address form inside the identification card, below the identifier boxes and above the save button — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:43-69, gated on the card's showAddress flag. The gate is the permanentAddress obligation in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:200-208, allow-listed to Cat and Dog in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:115. So the user meets the question once per animal, interleaved with that animal's identifiers, and answers it as many times as there are animals on the line. No frontend capture shows it: the corpus photographed cow, horse and fish, none of which is on the allow list.

DR1 gives it a page of its own, /permanent-address/select, headed "Permanent address" under the "Consignment parties" caption, reached from the roles-and-addresses list as a section beside consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination — app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:79-97 declares it, and :124-131 attaches it to commodity code 01061900, where it stands in place of the CPH row that cattle and pig notifications get, so that list is still six rows long. The page asks about every animal at once: one bordered card per animal, headed "Canis familiaris 1", "Canis familiaris 2", each card repeating that animal's already-entered identifiers in an inset so the user can tell them apart (app/views/permanent-address-animals.html:66-97), and one set of page-level Save and continue / Save and return buttons at the foot. The dr1-permanent-address-animals capture shows two dog cards on one page. DR1 asks the question for cat, dog and ferret, one commodity more than the frontend's two.

Move the question out of the identification card and onto a page of its own in the addresses part of the journey, listing every animal on every permanent-address commodity line at once. That means: a new page and route; a section row alongside the other consignment-party addresses, standing where the CPH row does on a cattle notification rather than beside it; removing the showAddress branch from _identification-card.njk:43-69 and the address fields from the identification card view model; and re-pointing the stored answer, which today hangs off the animal record as `permanentAddress` inside animalIdentifiers. The per-animal granularity does not change — DR1 asks per animal too — only where and how many at a time. Because the new page needs the animals to exist first, it has to sit after identification in the flow even though it belongs with the addresses; check the ordering against the hub task rows before building. Who the rule applies to is not part of this change: DR1's set is cat, dog and ferret against the frontend's cat and dog, and ferret is not in the frontend's commodity catalogue at all, so the allow list widens when the catalogue does and the catalogue finding already carries that dependency by name.

increments.title: DR1 lets the user reuse the place of destination as an animal's permanent address; the frontend makes them type a full address for every animal
increments.detail:
The frontend's permanent-address block offers no choice at all — it goes straight from the heading and the sentence "A permanent address is required for this animal." into nine empty address boxes, built by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/address/fields.js:117-163 and rendered by _identification-card.njk:43-69 in the same feature. There is no option to reuse an address already on the notification and no address-book picker, although the service has pickers for the consignee and the other party roles. A user importing four dogs to one destination types the same address four times. No frontend capture shows this: the block is gated to Cat and Dog and the corpus captured cow, horse and fish.

DR1 asks each animal "Select an address" and offers two radios. The first is "Same as the place of destination (POD)", hinted with the actual destination address the user already gave — the dr1-permanent-address-animals capture reads "Riverside Holding Facility, East Farm Road, Leeds, LS25 3EB, United Kingdom". The second is "Enter a new address", hinted "This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.", and it reveals the address form conditionally. The address form is only ever shown after the user has said they need one: app/views/permanent-address-animals.html:82-94.

Put a two-option radio ahead of the address form: reuse the place of destination, or enter a new address, with the new-address fields as a conditional reveal on the second. The destination address is already on the notification, so the hint text can be rendered from it; where no destination has been given yet DR1 blocks the reuse option with "Add a place of destination before you can continue" (app/routes.js:2682-2692), and the frontend needs the same guard. Storing the choice matters as much as showing it — DR1 keeps the choice and copies the destination address into the permanent-address answer rather than storing a pointer, so decide whether the frontend copies or references before building.

increments.title: The frontend offers "Save and add another" even when the line holds a single animal; DR1 hides that button and renames it "Save and finish" for the last animal
increments.detail:
The in-card action button always reads "Save and add another" and is always rendered while the card is below its cap — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:71-76 emits it unconditionally in the not-at-maximum branch. All three species captures show it against a line of one animal: fe-animal-identification and fe-animal-identification-horse and fe-animal-identification-fish each read "Enter details for … 1 of 1" and still offer to add another. Pressing it on such a line saves the animal and the card then re-renders in its maximum-reached state, so the label promises a second animal the line cannot hold and the user finds that out only after committing the first.

DR1 decides the in-card button per species panel in app/routes.js:1712-1721. When the line holds one animal the button is suppressed entirely and the user saves with the page-level Save and continue. When more than one animal remains the button reads "Save and add another", and on the last remaining animal it reads "Save and finish". The dr1-animal-identification-details capture is a two-animal line on its first animal, so it shows "Save and add another"; the one-animal and last-animal states were not photographed.

Drive the in-card button from the line's cap and the number of records already saved, in the card view model at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/card/view-model.js:84-118: no button when the cap is one, "Save and add another" while more than one animal remains, and a finish label on the last. Both strings the card would need already exist in the commodities copy file, and the submit value for the finish case is the action the page-level finish button already posts. The wording of the last-animal button has to be settled first: "Save and finish" is already this page's page-level primary button, so lifting it into the card puts two identically labelled buttons on one page. This is the button inside the species card, not the page-level save-and-return pattern.

increments.title: DR1's country list carries the 27 EU member states plus 11 EU overseas territories and 3 Crown Dependencies; the frontend offers 27 member states plus four EFTA countries and no territories at all, on both the origin and the destination question.
increments.detail:
Country of origin and Destination country both offer the same 31 entries: the 27 EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. No territory or Crown Dependency appears. Both pages read one function — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:57-61 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/controller.js:24-28 both call countries.originCountries() — and that is filled from the reference-data service's /countries endpoint for the GBNAG_SPS_EX block at src/server/app/services/countries/index.js:11. Three member states are also named differently from DR1: Czechia, Ireland and Netherlands (the).

The list is 41 entries, alphabetical, and the same list serves the origin question and both destination-country reveals. It is the 27 member states, then 11 EU overseas territories written as "territory (parent)" — Azores (Portugal), Canary Islands (Spain), Ceuta (Spain), French Guiana (France), Guadeloupe (France), Madeira (Portugal), Martinique (France), Mayotte (France), Melilla (Spain), Reunion (France), Saint Martin (France) — and 3 Crown Dependencies, Guernsey (United Kingdom), Isle of Man (United Kingdom) and Jersey (United Kingdom). It carries no EFTA country: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland are absent. DR1 names the member states Czech Republic, Republic of Ireland and Netherlands.

The list a user picks from has to become DR1's 41 entries, on both pages, including the parent country in each territory label. The frontend does not own the list — the names come from reference data's GBNAG_SPS_EX block — so the territories and Crown Dependencies must be added there first, each with the ISO code the region-of-origin prefix will use, and the four EFTA entries removed. Whether to follow DR1's naming of Czech Republic, Republic of Ireland and Netherlands is part of the same list decision. Because both pages read one function, the frontend side is a single change once the data exists.

No claim falsified. Two refinements, neither changing the slots. (1) The dependency is understated rather than wrong: reference-data does not own these names either — Country.java builds each entry from an MdmCountry (getEffectiveAlpha2 / getEffectiveAlias), so reference-data proxies DEFRA MDM and the territories have to reach MDM before reference-data can serve them. `needs-backend` is right and if anything the chain is one hop longer than the difference slot says. (2) Crop risk under rubric 8: on dr1-origin-of-the-import the name `countryOfOrigin` belongs to a hidden input (the search control writes into it), so a crop keyed on that name resolves to a zero-size box on the DR1 side. The frontend side crops fine.

DUPLICATE SWEEP: both findings survive, and this one must not be actioned on its own. transport--transit-country-list-membership describes the same two lists in different words — the same DR1 41 and the same frontend 31, down to the same three naming differences — because the transit-countries page reads the same function this one names. Checked rather than inferred: `countries.originCountries()` has exactly three callers in the whole app, origin/controller.js:60, destination-country/controller.js:27 and transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js:23, all fed from the one GBNAG_SPS_EX block at services/countries/index.js:24. So one data change closes three questions, and this finding's instruction to remove the four EFTA entries is the very change the transit finding bands `disputed` and argues is unsafe, on the ground that dropping Norway and Switzerland would stop a user recording the ordinary road route into GB. The two are not merged: they are one shared list carrying two questions that may legitimately want to diverge, and they sit either side of a band boundary. Whoever picks this up settles the transit finding's question first, or splits the list so the transit question stops borrowing the origin one.

Confirmed the three naming differences in the rendered markup — "Czechia" against "Czech Republic", "Ireland" against "Republic of Ireland", "Netherlands (the)" against "Netherlands". Opened both origin screenshots. Re-resolved all four citations: origin/controller.js:57-61 and destination-country/controller.js:24-28 are both the countryItems spread of countries.originCountries(), and services/countries/index.js:11 is the fetchCountries(['GBNAG_SPS_EX']) call. increments.title: DR1 asks for the country of origin with a type-ahead search box under its own "Country of origin" subheading; the frontend uses a plain dropdown the user must scroll.
increments.detail:
Country of origin is a govuk-select rendered from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/template.njk:15-22, labelled with a govuk-label--s label and opening on the placeholder "Select a country" followed by a disabled divider row. Country of origin sits under its own h2 subheading and is a search field — a text input placeheld "Search for a country" with a search button, which filters the country list as the user types and writes the chosen value into a hidden countryOfOrigin input. Only the destination-country question, which is a different control, uses a plain select in DR1.

Replace the origin country select with the same search-and-filter control, and promote its label to a subheading above the field. The prototype's version knows about parent countries — a territory is listed as "Azores (Portugal)" and carries Portugal as a parent — so the control should be built against a list of that shape rather than a flat one; that list is a separate finding and can land first or last. The frontend already ships a reusable type-ahead of this kind: src/server/common/components/accessible-autocomplete/macro.njk enhances a govukSelect into a type-ahead, and the port of entry field already uses it at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:18-27. Applying that macro to countryOfOrigin is the smallest version of this change. It gives type-ahead filtering but not DR1's exact presentation — DR1 renders a search input with a magnifier button and its own results list, not an enhanced select — so decide which of the two the service is adopting before building it.

increments.title: DR1 gives every question on the origin page the same medium subheading, so the page reads as three equally weighted questions; on the frontend two are small bold labels and the third is plain body text.
increments.detail:
The origin page asks three questions at three different weights. "Country of origin" is a govuk-label--s, "Does the consignment have a region of origin code?" is a govuk-fieldset__legend--s, and "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)" has no size class at all, so it renders at body weight and reads as a caption rather than a question. In the full-page shot the third question is visibly lighter than the two above it. The classes are set in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/template.njk:15-22 for the country, :36-44 for the region fieldset and :46-54 for the internal reference.

All three questions carry the same medium heading treatment and render at one size, larger than any of the frontend's three. "Country of origin" is an h2, "Does the consignment have a region of origin code?" is a legend--m and "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)" is a govuk-label--m, and all three also carry DR1's own app-eu-heading-m class. The wording of all three is identical to the frontend's, so nothing about the questions themselves differs — only their weight. DR1 uses this treatment on pages that ask several unrelated questions; it does not appear on single-question pages such as CPH number or consignment details.

Raise the three question labels on the origin page to a single consistent size: govuk-label--m on the internal reference, govuk-fieldset__legend--m on the region-of-origin fieldset, and the country label to match, so the page presents three questions of equal standing rather than a hierarchy the content does not have. increments.title: DR1 offers ten animal-approved border control posts as the port of exit; the frontend offers the whole 78-entry list of GB ports and airports, most of which cannot handle live animals.
increments.detail:
The Port of exit select lists 78 entries from Aberdeen Airport (GB DYC) to Tilbury Port (GB TILL) — every general GB port and airport, including places with no animal facilities such as Cambridge Airport and Nottingham Port. The options come from the ports-of-entry list, which the page reuses wholesale: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/controller.js:22-30 maps ports.list(), and src/server/app/services/ports/index.js:11 fills that from the reference-data service's /ports-of-entry endpoint. The hint says so out loud — "Choose where the consignment will leave Great Britain. Exit and entry share the same port list." — at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/copy/copy.en.js:5. The same 78-entry select is offered for transit and for temporary admission horses alike, and validation accepts any code in it: :32-38.

The Port of exit select offers ten options and each names the site and its animal BCP code, quoted here exactly as DR1 renders them: "Edinburgh Airport (animals) - GBEDI4", "Gatwick Airport (animals) - GBLGW4", "Glasgow Airport (animals) - GBGLA002", "Heathrow Airport - HARC (animals) - GBLHR4A", "Heathrow Airport – Airpets Limited (animals) – GBLHR022 - GBLHR022", "Heathrow Airport – Animal Aircare Ltd (animals) - GBLHR067", "Holyhead POE - GBHLY", "Manchester Airport (animals) - GBMNC4", "Prestwick Airport (animals) - GBPIK4" and "Stansted Airport (animals) - GBSTN4A". The Airpets entry repeats its code twice and three entries separate their parts with an en dash where the other seven use a hyphen; both are in DR1's own data, so whoever builds the real list should treat those two as DR1 errors to be tidied rather than copied. The same ten are offered under Transit and under Temporary admission horses. There is no hint on the field.

The exit port must be chosen from the animal-approved border control posts, not from the ports-of-entry list. Reference data has no such list today — the frontend's only source is /ports-of-entry — so a list of exit BCPs has to exist there first, keyed on the animal BCP codes DR1 shows, and the port-of-exit page then reads that instead of ports.list(). The hint sentence "Exit and entry share the same port list" goes with it, since it will no longer be true. Until reference data carries the list this cannot be finished in the frontend alone. Note also that DR1 labels each option with its BCP code, which the frontend's "(GB XXX)" suffix does not carry.

increments.title: DR1 asks the reason for import and everything that reason reveals on one page; the frontend sends the user through up to three further pages to answer the same follow-up questions.
increments.detail:
The user picks one of five reasons on its own page and presses Save and continue, and the follow-up questions arrive as separate pages afterwards, one field per page. Internal market leads to a Purpose in the internal market page; Transhipment or onward travel leads to a Destination country page; Transit leads to a Port of exit page and then a Destination country page; Temporary admission horses leads to an Exit date page and then a Port of exit page; Re-entry leads straight on. Each is a distinct route with its own heading and its own Save and continue, and each returns its own errors to itself. In the hub the five pages sit behind two rows, not five: "Main reason for importing" covers the reason and the internal-market purpose, and "Exit details" covers destination country, port of exit and exit date, and that second row stays "Cannot start yet" until the reason is answered. The five pages are declared as five entries in one flow section in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:48-58, and which of them a user meets is decided by the four gates in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:43-116.

DR1 asks all of it on /reason-for-import. The five reasons are radios, and four of them carry a govuk-radios conditional reveal that opens in place under the chosen option: Internal market reveals the eleven purpose radios, Transhipment or onward travel reveals Destination country, Transit reveals Port of exit and then Destination country, and Temporary admission horses reveals Exit date and then Port of exit. Re-entry reveals nothing. One Save and continue submits the reason and whatever it revealed together, and a missing answer inside a reveal is reported on the same page against the revealed field, as dr1-reason-for-import-error shows with the summary link "Select a purpose in the internal market" pointing at the internal-market radios inside the open reveal.

Fold the four follow-up pages back into the reason page as conditional reveals, so a user answers the reason and its consequences in one submit. The four gates already encode exactly the right conditions and do not change — this is a change of where the questions are rendered and validated, not of when they apply. The work is: render the purpose radios, destination country, port of exit and exit date as conditional HTML on the reason page in the order DR1 shows them (transit: port of exit above destination country; temporary admission: exit date above port of exit); validate reason and the revealed field in one pass and return errors against the revealed control; fold the hub's "Exit details" row into "Main reason for importing" so the two rows become one, which also retires the "Cannot start yet" state that row is the only user of; and adopt DR1's page heading, which is a separate finding because it can be done on its own. Purge-on-flip already drops answers that go out of scope when the reason changes, so no state work is implied. Do this before the smaller findings that edit those pages' controls, or expect to move that work twice.

increments.title: DR1 fills in the selected country's code as a fixed prefix and asks only for the part after it; the frontend asks the user to type the whole region of origin code into a field capped at five characters.
increments.detail:
Answering Yes reveals one text input labelled "Region of origin code", hinted "For example, FR-75", five characters wide and with no prefix shown. The user types the country part and the region part together, and the whole string is capped at five characters by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:37 and :71-75, whose error reads "Region of origin code must be 5 characters or less". The example in the hint, FR-75, is itself exactly five characters, so any code with a longer region part cannot be entered.

Answering Yes reveals a field labelled "Enter the region of origin code" hinted "Enter up to 5 characters.", with the selected country's code shown as a read-only prefix attached to the left of the input. The user types only the part after it and the prototype joins the two with a hyphen on submit. The prefix is looked up from the chosen country, so Ceuta (Spain) gives XC and Melilla (Spain) gives XL rather than the parent country's ES.

Split the field: show the selected country's code as a prefix and collect only the suffix, capping the suffix at five characters rather than the whole code. The stored value should still be the joined code, so nothing downstream needs to change shape. The prefix depends on knowing a code per country including the territories, which is where this meets the country-list finding — Ceuta and Melilla have their own prefixes, not their parent's. If the country control becomes a search box the prefix has to update as the search selection changes, not only on page load.

Transport and arrival" beside the port of entry itself. Both labels are DR1's, both are signed off, and they name different things.

increments.title: DR1 lets a user open the review page before the notification is finished and names every gap there — an error summary, a red message on each incomplete card and a marked-empty row for each missing answer; the frontend has no such state.
increments.detail:
The frontend has one review page and it has no incomplete presentation at all. The route is ungated — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/controller.js:94 hands the GET straight to the renderer with no readiness check — so a user who types the URL does reach it while the notification is unfinished. What they meet is the ordinary summary: every unanswered question reads "Not provided" in the same grey as a real answer, there is no error summary, no card is flagged, nothing distinguishes an answer the user chose to leave blank from one the service still needs, and the page ends with a live Continue button that says nothing about what is missing. The frontend does not offer that page from anywhere in the interface: the hub's "Check and submit" row is rendered as unlinked plain text reading "Cannot start yet" until the readiness gate passes (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:65 and :81-82, gated by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:82-85), and no answer page leads forward into review — every section returns to the hub. So the state exists but is unreachable by any route a user would find, and useless when reached.

DR1 treats the review page as the place gaps are reported. Opening it on an unfinished notification shows a "There is a problem" error summary above the heading listing one link per incomplete card — in the captured state "Complete additional details", "Complete arrival details", "Complete transport details", "Complete roles and addresses" and "Complete contact address for this consignment", each anchored to its card (app/views/review-notification.html:32-37). Each named card then carries a red left-hand bar, a red error message repeating the same sentence, and every one of its rows shows the label with a visibly empty value marked up as missing for screen readers (app/views/partials/review-summary-row.html:15-24). Complete cards are untouched. The Continue button stays, and posting it re-renders the same page with the same errors rather than moving on. The prototype has no equivalent of "Cannot start yet" — the string appears nowhere in it — and its hub offers an always-enabled "Review and submit" button.

Build the incomplete state on the review page: compute which cards are short of a required answer, render a govuk error summary listing one entry per incomplete card anchored to that card, put a govuk error message inside each affected card, and render each missing row with an empty value carrying a visually hidden "Missing" rather than the "Not provided" placeholder. Then open the route — remove the readiness gate from the review section so the page can be reached while incomplete — and keep the existing submission guard, which already refuses an unready notification (src/server/app/engine/write/submit.js:9-15), so opening the page cannot let an unfinished notification through. Whoever owns the hub has to change the "Check and submit" row at the same time, because leaving it as "Cannot start yet" would leave the new state unreachable; agree that with them before landing. This depends on the six-section layout only for which card an error attaches to, so it can be built after that lands.

increments.title: The frontend's review page shortens the means-of-transport row to "Means of transport"; DR1's review page repeats the question's own wording, "Means of transport to the port of entry".

The Arrival details card labels the row "Means of transport" against the value "Road Vehicle" — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:71. increments.title: DR1 lays the review page out as six numbered sections with a named subsection above every card; the frontend uses three, and files several answers under a different section from DR1.
increments.detail:
The frontend shows three numbered sections — "1. About the consignment", "2. Movement", "3. Addresses" — plus a conditional "4. Documents". Section 1 carries three plain group headings, "Consignment details", "Commodity details" and "Species", and under them three cards: "Import details", "Additional animal details" (which holds Certified for, Includes unweaned animals, Reason for import and Purpose in the market together) and one card per species titled "Cow (0102) — Bos taurus" (which holds commodity code, common name, species, number of animals, number of packages and the animal identifier table together). Section 2 holds "Arrival details" — with the transit countries as a row inside it — and "Transport details". Section 3 holds "Roles and addresses" and "Contact address for this consignment". The section and group names are fixed strings in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:35-44, and the three sections are assembled in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/index.js:15-21.

DR1 shows six numbered sections, each with a subsection heading above each card that names what the card answers — app/views/review-notification.html:40-176. They are: "1. About the consignment" ("Where is this consignment coming from?" → Import details; "What are you importing?" → Animal details; "Main reason for import" → Main reason for import); "2. Description of the goods" ("Commodity details" → a Commodity details card grouped by commodity; "Identification details" → one card per species carrying the animal table; "Additional details" → Certified for and Includes unweaned animals); "3. Transport and arrival" ("Arrival details"; an optional "Transit countries" card of its own; "Transport details"); "4. Documents" ("Upload documents" → Uploaded documents); "5. Consignment parties" ("Roles and addresses"); "6. Contact address" ("Contact address for this consignment"). So DR1 separates what the frontend fuses: reason for import gets its own card in section 1 rather than sharing one with the animal welfare answers; the commodity figures and the animal identifiers become two cards in section 2 rather than one; and transit countries become a card rather than a row.

Rebuild the section list to DR1's six, add the subsection heading above every card, and move four blocks of content: Reason for import and Purpose in the market out of the "Additional animal details" card into their own "Main reason for import" card in section 1; Certified for and Includes unweaned animals into an "Additional details" card in section 2; the animal identifier table out of the species card into an "Identification details" card in section 2, leaving the commodity figures behind in a "Commodity details" card; and the transit-countries row out of "Arrival details" into a card of its own. All of it is view-model and copy work in the check-answers feature — no answer is added or removed, only regrouped and relabelled — so it can land in one pass and its test is the rendered heading order. Land the page-heading change with it.

increments.title: Viewing an already-submitted notification, the frontend still shows "Now submit your notification" and a Continue button; DR1's read-only review drops the submit form.
increments.detail:
The read-only view of a Submitted notification is the same page with the Change links stripped: the tag turns green, "Copy as new" and "Delete" appear at the top, and every row loses its Change action. The submit block does not go with them. Below the last card the page still reads "Now submit your notification" / "Continue to the declaration to submit your notification." over a green Continue button, on a notification that was submitted already. The template renders that block unconditionally — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:108-114 sits outside any read-only test. The flag is computed in the controller and reaches the template, but the Change actions are stripped earlier, in the view model, so nothing at the foot of the page ever consults it. The button is not inert: it posts, and where the notification is still complete it moves the user forward towards the declaration again.

DR1 does define a read-only review, contrary to what the pairing note assumed: a notification the user submits in the prototype is stored in the session and the dashboard links it to /review-notification?submitted=<id>, which renders the same view with a read-only flag (app/routes.js:10024-10037). That flag does two things — it clears every card's change target, and it suppresses the submit form, because the form is wrapped in a not-read-only test in app/views/review-notification.html:181-187. So a submitted notification in DR1 ends after the last card, with nothing to press. Only DR1's eight seeded demonstration rows on the dashboard have a dead "View" link; a notification the user actually submitted gets a working one. This corpus captured no picture of that state, so the DR1 half of this finding is read from source rather than observed; the state that would settle it is /review-notification?submitted=<id> in the prototype, reached by completing the journey, confirming the declaration and following "View" on the dashboard row that appears.

Wrap the "Now submit your notification" heading, its sentence and the Continue form in the same read-only test that already hides the Change actions, so the block disappears for a Submitted notification and the page ends after the last card. One template change. It is worth checking every other status the frontend renders this page in — Amending in particular — so the block is suppressed exactly where there is nothing left to submit.

increments.title: DR1 shows "Not applicable" against a question the notification never had to answer; the frontend shows "Not provided", which reads as an omission.

Every blank value on the review page renders as "Not provided" — three times on the captured page, against Region of origin code, Internal reference number and Number of packages. "Not provided" reads as a reproach: it tells the user something was expected of them and they did not do it, even where the question never applied.

DR1 renders the same rows as "Not applicable" — app/routes.js:4065-4070 — which says the opposite: the question had no bearing on this notification and no action is owed. DR1 keeps a separate treatment, an empty value marked "Missing", for a value the service actually still needs, and uses it only inside a card the error summary has already flagged. So the two cases a user can be in are told apart by the words on the page.

Replace the single "Not provided" string with "Not applicable" for a question that did not apply, in both the English and Welsh copy. Keep it distinct from the missing-value treatment that the incomplete review state introduces, so the page never uses one form of words for both a question that was never asked and one that still needs an answer.

increments.title: The frontend shows a breadcrumb trail above the back link on 34 screens and an empty one on the dashboard; DR1 uses no breadcrumbs anywhere.
increments.detail:
37 of the 40 captured screens render a breadcrumb trail — "Your notifications" then the page name — from `src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:42-48`. On 34 of them it sits directly above a "Back" link, so the page offers a user two competing ways back at the same time. The three task-list screens are the only ones that suppress it. On both dashboard captures the trail renders as an empty navigation landmark: a navigation region labelled "Breadcrumb" containing a list with no items in it at all, which a screen reader announces as a navigation region a user can enter and find nothing in.

No DR1 screen shows breadcrumbs, and no view in the prototype references the component. Every DR1 page that needs a way back offers the back link alone, directly under the phase banner — `app/views/declaration.html:21-24`.

Remove the breadcrumb trail from the shared layout and keep the back link, which is what DR1 shows on every page and what the GOV.UK Design System asks for: its breadcrumbs guidance says not to use breadcrumbs and a back link on the same page. Doing this removes the frontend's only standing route back to the notification list, so it should land with the service-navigation menu, whose Dashboard item is DR1's route back. If the trail is kept instead, the empty one on the dashboard has to go regardless — an empty navigation landmark is a defect on its own terms and needs no design decision.

increments.title: The frontend still shows the blue Draft tag and the notification reference above the heading on the declaration page; DR1 clears that strip away for the declaration.

The declaration page opens with the same status strip every other journey page carries — a blue "Draft" tag beside the notification reference — sitting between the back link and the "Declaration" heading. The submitted page drops it too, and there the reference moves into the confirmation panel instead.

Stop rendering the status strip on the declaration page, so the page starts at its heading as DR1's does. The strip is not built in the shared layout unconditionally — it is built from what the page passes in — so this is a change to what the declaration's render supplies, not a change to the layout, and no other page is touched. increments.title: The frontend lets a user save and leave from every journey question page; DR1 offers that on most of its pages but not on seven of them, and DR1 does not say which is right.
increments.detail:
Every journey page that offers a save action offers the same three, from one shared partial (`src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13`): a primary "Save and continue", a secondary "Save and return to hub" and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. That is 24 of the 40 captured screens. Sixteen do not carry them, and eleven of those are pages where they would make no sense — the three task-list states, the two dashboards, the review, the declaration, the confirmation, the check-answers pair and the delete and cancel-amend confirmations. That leaves one group of journey question pages that asks a question and offers no way to save and leave: the five address pickers, which end with "Save and continue" on its own.

DR1 offers the equivalent pair on 26 of its 42 screens. Sixteen do not carry it, and nine of those are again pages where it would make no sense — the four dashboard states, the task list, the declaration, the submitted page and the two review states. The remaining seven are journey question pages, and they end in three different ways. Origin of the import and CPH number end with "Save and continue" alone (`app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:167-175`). The address select page ends with "Save and continue" and a secondary "Add a new address". The two add-a-transporter detail forms, commercial and private, end with "Save and continue" and a secondary "Cancel and return to dashboard" — which returns to the notification list, not to the task list. The transporter-type page and the contact address page end with a bare "Continue". Set against the pairing, five pairs that match screen for screen diverge: origin, CPH number, transporter type, the private transporter form and the contact address page all let a frontend user save and leave where their DR1 counterpart does not. The address pickers are not among them, because neither side offers it there.

There is nothing to build until somebody says which side is right, which is why this is banded disputed rather than as work. DR1 is not consistent with itself here: 26 of its pages carry the pair and seven journey question pages do not, and nothing in the evidence separates the two groups — they are not one section, not one journey branch, and not one kind of question. DR1 is not even consistent within the seven: two end with "Save and continue" alone, two end with "Save and continue" and a cancel that goes to the dashboard rather than the task list, one adds an unrelated secondary, and two end with a bare "Continue" that does not use the word save at all. The frontend's behaviour is a superset of DR1's rather than a contradiction of it, so removing the actions from those five pages would make the service worse if DR1's omission is drift rather than intent. What settles it: a designer saying whether every journey page should let a user save and return to the task list, or whether those specific pages are deliberately continue-only. If the answer is "every page", DR1 needs updating and the frontend is already correct; if it is "only some", the rule that picks them needs writing down before anything is removed, and it has to account for the four wordings DR1 uses across the seven.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a "Save and return to overview" action on DR1's origin of the import, CPH number or add-a-private-transporter pages.

Only five of the 40 captured screens show anything above the page heading: the address pickers, which print "Consignment addresses" in a `govuk-caption-l` from `src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.njk:7`. That is the only caption in the whole frontend. On every other journey page the slot above the heading holds either nothing or the journey strip — a blue "Draft" tag beside the notification reference, `src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:64-69` — so a user part-way through a notification is never told on the page itself which section of the task list they are working in.

36 of DR1's 42 screens print a caption immediately above the heading, and on 32 of those it names the part of the notification. Read from the rendered DOM, the captions are "About the consignment" on eleven screens (origin of the import, what are you importing and its results, reason for import with its error state and its four revealed states, consignment details, animal identification), "Consignment parties" on six (roles and addresses in its three states, consignment address select, CPH number, permanent address), "Documents" on all seven upload states, "Add a new transporter" on the three add-a-transporter pages, "Transport and arrival" on two (transporter, arrival details), "Movement" on two (transit countries, empty and selected) and "Commodity details" on one (additional animal details). The remaining four are the dashboard's own "Dashboard", which names the page rather than a part of a notification and is covered by the dashboard title finding. `app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:39-40` shows the pattern: a caption paragraph then the heading. The six DR1 screens with nothing above the heading are the declaration, the submitted page, the two review states, the contact address page and the notification hub.

Add a caption above the heading on each journey page naming the section it belongs to, taking the wording from DR1 page by page. Two of DR1's captions do not agree with DR1's own task-list section headings — it captions the additional animal details page "Commodity details" where its task list says "2. Description of the goods", and the transit countries page "Movement" where its task list says "3. Transport and arrival" — and those two need a designer's word before they are copied across, because the frontend's own task list happens to use "Commodity details" and "Movement" as its section names. The other captions can be copied as they stand. This is independent of any work on what the task-list sections are called.

increments.title: DR1 puts a Dashboard, Address book, Manage account and Log out menu in the service navigation on every page; the frontend's service navigation carries only the service name.
increments.detail:
On all 40 captured screens the service navigation strip holds the words "Import notification service" and nothing else — `src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:27-32` passes the component a service name and a service URL but no navigation items. Underneath it a separate right-aligned strip shows the signed-in user's email address and a "Sign out" link (`src/server/common/components/service-header/template.njk`). There is no link to an address book and no link to account settings anywhere in the chrome, and the only standing route back to the list of notifications is the breadcrumb.

All 42 DR1 screens carry a four-item menu in the service navigation: Dashboard, Address book, Manage account, Log out, with the item you are on marked as current. It is declared in the service's own layout, `app/views/layouts/main.html:99-125`, so it is a decision of this design rather than something the Prototype Kit supplies. Dashboard points at the notification list and Address book at `/address-book`; Manage account and Log out are left as `#` placeholders in the prototype.

Pass a navigation array to the service-navigation component in the shared layout and mark the active item. Dashboard and Log out have frontend destinations already — the notification list at `/` and the sign-out route the existing strip uses — so those two can be wired straight away. Address book and Manage account have no page in this frontend today, so they either wait for those destinations or ship as the same placeholders DR1 uses; that is a call for whoever owns the roadmap, not a blocker on the menu itself. Once Log out is in the menu, the separate user-and-sign-out strip is doing only one job, showing who is signed in, and should be reviewed against DR1, which shows no signed-in identity at all.

increments.title: DR1's submitted page tells the user what is still outstanding before the consignment is imported; the frontend's confirmation page says nothing about it.
increments.detail:
After submitting, the page runs from the green confirmation panel straight to a date of declaration and then "Transporting the consignment" (`src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/confirmation/template.njk:11-13`). Nothing on the page, and no key in its copy file, tells the user that anything is still owed. A notification can reach this page with no documents uploaded at all — the documents obligation allows nought to ten with no minimum (`src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:19-28`) — so a user can submit without the health certificate and be told nothing.

DR1 shows a "Before the consignment is imported" section immediately under the panel, introduced by "You still need to:" and listing what is outstanding for this particular notification. The two lines it can show are "upload the health certificate and any other required documents", when nothing has been uploaded, and "complete the animal identifier information in the notification", when identifiers are required and the minimum for submitting has been met but not all of them are filled in (`app/views/notification-submitted.html:27-37`). The section is not rendered when the list is empty, so a complete notification sees the page the frontend shows today.

Add the section to the confirmation page, built from the notification's own state at the moment of submission, and suppress it when the list comes back empty. The first line needs only a check of whether any document was saved, which the frontend already holds. The second line needs the frontend to decide what "the minimum for submitting" means for animal identifiers — its own gate onto this page is a roll-up of task-row statuses rather than a per-animal count — so if that question is not yet settled, ship the documents line first and add the identifier line when it is. No backend change is involved either way: both facts are already in the saved notification.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding that the frontend refuses to submit a notification with no documents uploaded, which would leave DR1's first outstanding-task line with nothing to report.

increments.title: DR1 gives its tables, summary cards and task list the full width of the page; the frontend squeezes the same content into a two-thirds column on every screen but the notification list.
increments.detail:
Every page in the journey renders its content in a two-thirds column, so nothing a user meets is ever wider than about 630 pixels of a 960-pixel container. The width is decided once, for the whole service, by the shared page base (`src/server/app/shared/kit.js:113-124`), which hard-codes the narrow surface and gives no page a way to ask for anything else; the shared layout then prints it (`src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:57`). The frontend already knows the wide surface exists — `kit.js:20-23` names both, `form` and `display` — and exactly one page uses it: the notification list, which passes `display` from its own controller (`src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:70`). Everything else inherits the narrow one, whatever it holds. The effect is worst where the content is tabular: the check-your-answers summary cards, the task list, the document table, the address picker and the animal identification cards all render at the width of a paragraph, so values wrap onto three and four lines and the page grows correspondingly long.

DR1 decides width per page and per element rather than once for the service. Its prose and its form fields are held to about 630 pixels wherever they appear, the same as the frontend, but anything tabular is given the whole 960-pixel container. Fifteen of the 42 DR1 screens render content wider than the frontend can: the two review states (`app/views/review-notification.html:28`), the notification hub, all seven upload-documents states, the transporter directory, the commodity details table, the animal identification cards, the address select list and the permanent address cards. On several of those the same page does both — the upload-documents intro wraps at 630 and the File upload card beneath it runs the full 960.

Let a page choose its content surface, and choose the wide one where DR1 does. The mechanism is already built and already proven on one page, so the work is to stop the shared base hard-coding `SURFACES.form` — take the surface as an option defaulting to `form` — and then pass `display` from the controllers of the pages DR1 renders wide: check your answers, the task list, documents, the address pickers, animal identification, commodity details and the transporter list. Nothing else changes: no copy, no fields, no routes, and the narrow surface stays the default so any page not named keeps the width it has today. Worth doing as one change rather than page by page, because the reason it is wrong everywhere is that it is decided in one place.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a frontend journey page whose content renders wider than the two-thirds column, or finding that DR1's wide pages are wide only because of the Prototype Kit's own layout rather than their own markup.

increments.title: DR1 asks for the means of transport with a dropdown; the frontend asks with four radios.
increments.detail:
Under the legend "Means of transport to the port of entry" the four options are laid out as radios, all visible without opening anything: Airplane, Railway, Road Vehicle, Vessel (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:29-39).

The same four options sit in a select that opens on "Select one" (app/views/arrival-details.html:110-120). The labels and their order are identical to the frontend's.

Nothing about the question, the options or their wording differs — only the control. Replace the four radios with a select that opens on "Select one", keeping the four labels and their order. Worth flagging to the designer when the work is picked up: a four-option question sits inside the range where the GOV.UK Design System asks for radios, and DR1 uses radios for every other short option set in the service, so the select on this one field may be an oversight in the signed-off design rather than an intention. That is a question about DR1, not about whether the frontend currently matches it.

increments.title: DR1 lets the user add a commercial transporter that is not already in the directory; on the frontend a commercial transporter can only be picked from a fixed list, so an unlisted one cannot be used at all.
increments.detail:
Choosing "Commercial" leads to a list of approved commercial transporters and nothing else. There is no "Add" control on that page and no route to one — the transporter part of the transport feature holds exactly three pages: the type question, the commercial pick-list and the private-transporter form (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/page.js:11-25). The list itself is a fixed pair of records held in the frontend (src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:6-27). A user whose commercial transporter is not in the list is stuck: the only way onward is to declare the transporter private, which is a different answer to a different question.

The transporter directory carries an "Add a transporter" secondary button below the list (app/views/transporter.html:160-165). It leads to "Choose a transporter type", warning "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first" and offering Private transporter or Commercial, where Commercial is hinted "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland". Choosing Commercial gives an "Add commercial transporter" page holding: an "Important — Help with transporter authorisation" panel repeating the DAERA/APHA authorisation rules; Transporter authorisation number; Name or organisation name; Address line 1; Address line 2 (optional); Town or city; County (optional); Postcode or Zip code; Country, which is locked to Northern Ireland and cannot be changed; then under an "Enter contact details" heading, Email address and Phone number. The added transporter joins the directory with the "New" status the list shows.

Build the add-a-transporter branch: an "Add a transporter" button on the commercial list, the type question as a branch of that button rather than as the section's entry, and an "Add commercial transporter" page carrying the fields above. The private form the frontend already has answers DR1's private branch. This depends on the transporter list becoming something a user can add to rather than a fixed list in the frontend, which is the same dependency as the "New" status tag. It also depends on the finding about where the type question sits, because DR1's add journey starts from the directory. One detail of DR1's page must not be copied without asking first: DR1 locks the new transporter's country to Northern Ireland and hints "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland", yet the directory that page adds to already holds commercial transporters from Romania, the Republic of Ireland, Denmark and Portugal — transporters that page could never have created. Build the page with an ordinary country field until a designer settles which of the two DR1 means.

increments.title: The two sides offer different places as the port of entry: DR1 searches 213 UK airports and seaports including Belfast, Larne and Warrenpoint; the frontend searches 78 Great Britain ports and airports and no Northern Ireland location at all.
increments.detail:
The port field is an autocomplete over a 78-entry list held as captured reference data (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json). Every entry is in Great Britain and every one reads as a place a consignment is inspected — Felixstowe Port, Port of Dover (Eastern), Heathrow Airport, Grimsby and Immingham Port — labelled "Name (CODE)" with a spaced UN/LOCODE.

The port field searches a 213-entry list (app/views/arrival-details.html:67) that is two datasets joined: twenty-eight UK airports labelled with IATA codes — "London Heathrow - LHR" — followed by the UK seaport gazetteer labelled with UN/LOCODEs — "Aberdeen - GBABD". It includes Northern Ireland — Belfast, Belfast International, Belfast City, Kilkeel, Larne, Londonderry, Warrenpoint — and small harbours such as Plockton, Kettletoft on Sanday and Pierowall on Westray.

Settle which list is right before changing the frontend, because adopting DR1's would let a user name a place the consignment cannot lawfully enter at. DR1's own page asks where the transporter "will enter with the consignment", and a live-animal consignment must arrive at a border control post; its list is a general UK ports-and-airports gazetteer, not a border-control-post list, and it offers Northern Ireland arrivals that cannot be a Great Britain point of entry for this notification. The frontend's 78 read as the border-control-post set and come from real reference data rather than a hardcoded page list. What settles it: the authoritative list of points of entry a live-animal consignment may be notified against, and whether Northern Ireland arrivals are in scope for this service at all. If DR1's breadth is intended, the frontend's reference data is the thing that changes, not the page.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any Northern Ireland location, or any harbour with no border control post, in the frontend's port list — its 78 entries are captured in full in the rendered select on fe-arrival-details and contain none.

increments.title: The frontend's port list shows a misspelt "Teestort", a shouted "TILBURY", a "Portsmouth  Port" with a doubled space and "Port of Sheerness" twice under the same code; DR1 shows each of those places once and spelt correctly.
increments.detail:
Five of the 78 port names a user reads are malformed (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:256-304). "Teesport" is spelt "Teestort". "Tilbury" is rendered "TILBURY" in capitals while two neighbouring entries read "Tilbury Port" and "Tilbury 2 Ro-Ro Terminal"; because the list is sorted by name, the capitals also throw it three rows away from them, above "Teesside International Airport". "Portsmouth  Port" carries two spaces between the words. Sheerness appears twice, both labelled "Port of Sheerness", under the codes "GBSHS" and "GB SHS" — the same code with and without its space, so the two options differ on screen by nothing but that space. And Pembroke appears twice, both labelled "Pembroke Port", under "GB PED" and "GB PEM".

DR1's port list carries "Teesport - GBTEE", "Tilbury - GBTIL" and "Sheerness - GBSHS", each spelt in sentence case and each appearing once, and carries no Pembroke or Portsmouth entry at all (app/views/arrival-details.html:67).

Correct the five labels: spell Teesport, put Tilbury in sentence case, remove the doubled space in Portsmouth Port, and collapse the duplicate Sheerness and Pembroke rows onto one code each. This is a data fix, not a page change, and it does not land in the frontend. The list is fetched at runtime from the reference-data service (src/server/app/services/ports/client.js), which serves it straight from DEFRA's master data (PortsOfEntryController -> MdmService in trade-imports-reference-data); the copy committed under the frontend's _capture fixtures is only the stub seed, so editing it corrects the local stack and nothing else. Raise the corrections against the master data. Worth doing whichever way the wider question about the port list is settled, though if that question replaces the dataset outright it goes with it.

increments.title: DR1 has the user add transit countries one at a time by searching, and lists what they added with a Remove link beside each; the frontend offers a flat list of 31 checkboxes, so the order the consignment passes through is never recorded.
increments.detail:
Under the label "Select all countries the consignment will travel through" the page renders every country as a checkbox in one alphabetical column, thirty-one of them from Austria to Switzerland, and the user scrolls and ticks (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js:22-27). What is stored is a set, deduplicated and unordered (:61-65). There is no search, nothing shows back which countries have been chosen apart from the ticks themselves, and there is nothing to remove — a user un-ticks. The page asks "Enter a country", hinted "Enter each country that the consignment will travel through", over a single search box placeholdered "Search for a country" (app/views/transit-countries.html:56-115). Each country the user picks is appended to a list below headed "Country", one row each, with a "Remove" link on the right. The list keeps the order they were added in, and the review page prints them in that order.

Replace the checkbox list with a country search that appends to a growing, removable list, and store the answer as an ordered sequence rather than a set. This changes what the answer means as well as how it is collected, so the stored shape and anything that reads it — the hub, the review page, the submitted payload — has to accept an ordered list. It travels with the two findings about the rules the frontend puts on this field, since all three change the same control.

increments.title: DR1 lets a rail or road consignment be saved with no transit countries at all; the frontend refuses the page until at least one country is chosen.
increments.detail:
The transited-countries obligation is gated on the means of transport being rail or road, and where it applies its status is mandatory (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/transport.js:93-104). Submitting the page with nothing ticked is rejected with "Select at least one country the consignment will travel through" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js:38-40). A consignment that crosses no third country — a lorry from the Republic of Ireland, say — has no honest answer to give, and the hub cannot be completed without one.

DR1 puts the page in the journey under the same condition, when the means of transport is Railway or Road Vehicle, and then lets it be left empty: the handler for the page saves whatever was submitted and redirects onward without validating anything, so pressing Save and continue with no country added takes the user to the next page (app/routes.js:10503-10537). Submission is not blocked either — the review card for transit countries is built with its error state permanently off, under the line "Transit countries are optional for submission" (:4795-4805). DR1 does not call an empty answer finished, though: its hub row for Transit countries reads "To do" until at least one country has been added (:5798-5802). The captured empty state shows Save and continue live with no country in the list.

Drop the at-least-one rule so the page can be saved and left with nothing chosen, and let a rail or road notification reach submission with no transit countries recorded. The gate itself — rail or road only — already matches DR1 and does not change, and neither does the hub: both sides leave the row outstanding while the list is empty, so it is the page and the submission that differ, not the task list. This should land with the change to the control, since both alter the same field. Neither side's captured screen shows the state after pressing Save and continue with nothing chosen, so the claim rests on reading the frontend's validator and DR1's route handler; photographing both sides at that moment would put it beyond argument.

increments.title: The two sides offer different countries as places a consignment can travel through: DR1 lists 41, including French Guiana, Réunion, Mayotte and the Channel Islands but not Norway or Switzerland; the frontend lists 31, the EU 27 plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.
increments.detail:
The checkboxes are drawn from the frontend's origin-country list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js:22-27). Thirty-one entries: the twenty-seven EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. No overseas territory or Crown Dependency appears, and no country outside the EU and EFTA does either. Three labels differ from DR1's for the same place — "Czechia", "Ireland" and "Netherlands (the)".

The search is fed a forty-one entry list (app/views/transit-countries.html:75). It holds the twenty-seven EU member states, eleven EU outermost regions and overseas entities — Azores, Canary Islands, Ceuta, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Madeira, Martinique, Mayotte, Melilla, Réunion, Saint Martin — and three Crown Dependencies, Guernsey, Isle of Man and Jersey. Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland are absent. The United Kingdom is absent too, matching the page's own line "This does not include the United Kingdom".

Settle which list is right before changing either side, because taking DR1 literally would both add and remove countries and each direction looks wrong on its face. DR1's own copy defines these as "countries between the country of origin and the destination country" — a consignment does not travel through Réunion, Mayotte, Martinique or French Guiana on its way to Great Britain, so DR1's data contradicts DR1's sentence; and dropping Switzerland and Norway would stop a user recording the most ordinary road route into GB from southern Europe. What settles it is the authoritative list of countries a consignment may be recorded as transiting — the same list the backend validates the submitted notification against — and a decision on whether one shared country list can serve both "where is this party's address" and "where does the consignment pass through", which is what put the territories in DR1's transit list in the first place. On the frontend the two questions already share one list too, so the change is not local to this page.

increments.detail:
The transporter section opens with "What type of transporter will move the animals?" and two radios — Commercial, hinted "A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list", and Private, hinted "You or another individual moving the animals — you will give their address" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:78-87). The answer routes the user to one of two pages that offer no way back to the other and no way to add anything: a commercial-only pick list, or an empty private-transporter form (obligations/sections/transport.js:33-62 makes the two mutually exclusive, purging the commercial answer when the type flips to Private and the reverse). A private transporter the user has used before must be typed in again, and a commercial one can never be typed in at all.

The section opens on the directory itself — "Transporter details", then "Select a transporter" over one table that mixes Commercial and Private rows and marks which is which in a Type column (app/views/transporter.html:113-153). The user picks a row. The type question exists only behind the "Add a transporter" button, where its heading is "Choose a transporter type" under the caption "Add a new transporter", it is preceded by the warning "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first", it lists Private transporter before Commercial, and its Commercial option carries an entirely different meaning: "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland".

Move the transporter section's entry from the type question to the directory, and make the directory hold private transporters as well as commercial ones. The type question becomes a step inside the add journey, reworded to DR1's heading and hints and with Private listed first. Everything a user does today stays reachable — choosing from the commercial list becomes choosing a Commercial row, and entering a private transporter becomes adding one — but both now start from the list. Do this before the add-a-commercial-transporter finding, which hangs off the same button.
